short_comment: Knight carried the ball seven times for 35 yards and caught his only target for 10 yards in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City.
long_comment: Although he split the backfield workload nearly equally with Tyler Allgeier, Knight was the more productive RB, although he still failed to reach 50 rushing yards for a fourth straight game. The 25-year-old running back gets a more favorable matchup in Week 12 against the Commanders, but Knight and Allgeier could face additional competition for touches if Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is cleared to return.

short_comment: Allgeier carried the ball seven times for 23 yards in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City.
long_comment: Game script fairly quickly put the Cardinals' running game in mothballs, and Allgeier wound up splitting the backfield workload nearly equally with Bam Knight, who picked up 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches. Allgeier has gone three straight games without reaching 50 rushing yards or getting into the end zone, but those games were also against very tough opponents (the Seahawks in Week 9, and the Rams in Week 10). The fifth-year RB could find a little more running room in Week 12 against the Commanders, but Jeremiyah Love (ankle) might also be ready to rejoin the lineup by then.

short_comment: Johnson completed 18 of 31 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City. he added five yards on two carries.
long_comment: The 40-year-old QB was pressed into duty with rookie Carson Beck (back) on the shelf, and Johnson unsurprisingly wasn't really up to the task after the Cardinals fell into a 14-0 hole before the first quarter was over. Johnson spent most of his afternoon finding Trey McBride for short gains, and he did hit Simi Fehoko for a two-yard score in the second quarter. Beck doesn't figure to miss much time, but if Johnson gets another start in Week 12, he'll be taking on a much less formidable Commanders' defense.

short_comment: McBride caught nine of 14 targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City. He added four yards on his only carry.
long_comment: Working with his fourth quarterback of the season in Josh Johnson, McBride dominated the 40-year-old's attention as no other Cardinal got more than seven targets or hauled in more than four passes. The star tight end wasn't able to do much with the volume, however, as his longest gain went for a mere nine yards. Carson Beck (back) could be back under center in Week 12 against the Commanders, but that might not improve McBride's outlook, as he saw only five targets in Week 10 during the rookie QB's first NFL start.

short_comment: Simon (calf) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
long_comment: Simon is being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's contest. His absence gives the Cardinals less depth at linebacker behind Jack Gibbens, Mack Wilson and Zaven Collins.

short_comment: The Cardinals elevated Jones from the practice squad Saturday.
long_comment: The veteran wideout played seven offensive snaps in Arizona's loss to the Rams last Sunday. With a boatload of injuries at the position, Jones figures to have a role for the foreseeable future. He has no fantasy appeal in this injury-ruined offense.

short_comment: Beck (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Kansas City, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
long_comment: The Cardinals were already preparing for Josh Johnson to operate as the starting quarterback Sunday, as Beck entered the weekend with the questionable tag due to back spasms. Joey Aguilar will operate as Johnson's backup, and Beck's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Froholdt (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
long_comment: Froholdt was a full practice participant both Thursday and Friday, and he's progressed enough in his recovery to clear the league's concussion protocol. With Jon Gaines (ankle) ruled out, Froholdt should reclaim his starting job at center for Sunday's road tilt.

short_comment: Carter (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports.
long_comment: Carter opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a knee injury he picked up in training camp in early August. He logged a trio of full practices during Week 11 prep but is not quite ready to return, so his next chance to make his 2026 debut is Week 12 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Williams (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
long_comment: Williams appears ready to return after missing the previous two games. He's been working as the Cardinals' starting left tackle after Paris Johnson (biceps) went on injured reserve following Week 4.

short_comment: Nolen (illness) was a full participant in practice Thursday, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports.
long_comment: The defensive tackle was not able to practice Wednesday due to an illness. Now that he's back, he should be able to play Sunday against the Chiefs. Nolen has played on a majority of the defensive snaps in each game he's been available for this season, recording 25 tackles (eight solo), including 1.0 sacks.

short_comment: Baker posted six tackles (two solo) during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams in Week 10.
long_comment: It was the third consecutive week that Baker recorded at least six stops (and the sixth time this season). The veteran safety is up to 68 tackles (31 solo), including a career-high 3.5 sacks, four pass defenses (including one interception) and one forced fumble through 10 regular-season games. Baker was held out of Wednesday's practice for rest purposes, so he should be available for Sunday's road game against the Chiefs.

short_comment: Wilson registered 10 tackles (six solo) during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams in Week 10.
long_comment: The Cardinals were blown out at home in Week 10, but Wilson came away from the loss with a season-high 10 stops while playing every single defensive snap. The veteran linebacker is up to 72 total tackles through 10 regular-season games, and he is three stops shy from matching his career-high that he set in 2024 with the Cardinals (over 16 regular-season contests).

short_comment: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that he has no new updates on the status of Conner (foot), who is still "working to return to perform," Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports. "It was not a good injury," LaFleur said.
long_comment: Conner hasn't played in a game since Week 3 of last season, when he sustained a right foot/ankle injury that required surgery. Though he was able to participate in individual drills in training camp, he never advanced to team work before being placed on injured reserve with a designation to return Aug. 30. The Cardinals still haven't cleared Conner to practice nearly three months later, which suggests that he either experienced a setback over the summer or plateaued in his recovery. Whatever the case, Conner doesn't seem close to a return, and the chances of him playing at any point this season will grow dimmer with each week that he doesn't practice.

short_comment: Wallace recorded a nine-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
long_comment: Though he played just five of the Cardinals' 35 snaps on offense, Wallace was able to come away with his first NFL reception in the third quarter. Even if Wallace earns more playing time in future weeks, he'll likely struggle to produce meaningful fantasy lines while rookie third-round pick Carson Beck continues to direct the offense behind a shaky offensive line.

short_comment: Minshew (elbow) underwent UCL reconstructive surgery Monday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Though the procedure will bring an end to Minshew's season, he's expected to make a full recovery ahead of the 2027 campaign. The veteran quarterback sustained the injury while making his lone start of the season Week 9 in Seattle, but he played though the elbow issue and completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards. Rookie third-round pick Carson Beck took over as the Cardinals' starting quarterback in Week 10 and is expected to lead the offense for the remainder of the season.

short_comment: The Cardinals placed Burch (knee) on injured reserve Tuesday.
long_comment: This move was a foregone conclusion, as head coach Mike LaFleur said Monday that Burch will miss the remainder of the campaign after suffering an MCL injury to his left knee. The defensive end finished his sophomore NFL season with 19 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, over 10 games. Burch will now look to get healthy in the hope of being ready for the 2027 campaign.

short_comment: Higgins played 24 of 35 offensive snaps (68.6 percent) but didn't get a target during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
long_comment: Week 10 was Higgins' first game since signing a three-year contract extension worth up to $26.8 million. He didn't have much to show for it during Sunday's loss, although the Cardinals finished with a measly 17:37 time of possession, and the offense struggled as a whole with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center. Higgins will take an 18-162-1 receiving line on 20 targets through 10 games into Arizona's Week 11 tilt against Kansas City on Nov. 22.

short_comment: Duvernay caught two of three targets for 35 yards during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
long_comment: Duvernay was on the field for only 10 of the Cardinals' 35 offensive snaps (28.6 percent), but the veteran wide receiver connected with rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck on passes of four and 31 yards on back-to-back plays late in the first quarter. Duvernay finished the contest second in catches, targets and receiving yards behind Trey McBride, and he's caught two passes in each of his last three outings. With Michael Wilson (neck) out for the year, the Cardinals' top wideouts for the rest of the season appear to be Duvernay, Simi Fehoko and rookie fifth-rounder Reggie Virgil, which doesn't inspire much confidence heading into Week 11 against Kansas City on Nov. 22.

short_comment: Hellams logged 11 tackles (seven solo) in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
long_comment: Hellams racked up tackles in what ended up being a disastrous night for the Falcons' defense. It's typically not a good thing when your third-level defender has to make all the plays, but make them, Hellams did, saving several explosive plays from the Chiefs' offense from becoming house calls.

short_comment: Zaccheaus caught two of his four targets for 17 yards and returned five punts for 81 yards during Atlanta's loss Sunday versus the Chiefs.
long_comment: Zaccheaus recorded a season-high 17 receiving yards during the loss while playing 29 snaps on offense and 14 on special teams. The 29-year-old has hauled in eight passes for 43 yards in addition to amassing 231 kick-return yards and 81 punt-return yards across nine games this season.

short_comment: Herbert caught two of his three targets for seven yards during Sunday's 35-13 loss versus the Chiefs. He also returned six kickoffs for 168 yards.
long_comment: Herbert was targeted three times for the second straight game in Week 10, but he continued to make a bigger impact on special teams. His first kickoff return of the day went for 39 yards to Atlanta's 45-yard line, but the offense promptly went three and out. He'll be hoping to keep up the momentum as a returner following the Falcons' bye in Week 11.

short_comment: Dotson caught three passes for 63 yards on six targets in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.
long_comment: Dotson has yet to hit 100 receiving yards in a game this season and has just two touchdowns, but he leads the league averaging 21.9 yards per catch, turning his 19 grabs into 416 yards through 10 games. He's fighting for leftover opportunities behind Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts in Atlanta's offense. Dotson isn't a reliable fantasy option down the stretch and headed into the Falcons' Week 11 bye.

short_comment: Moody went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.
long_comment: Moody was signed by the Falcons off the Ravens' practice squad Tuesday, and he was able to put together a perfect debut with the team in Week 10. The kicker converted a 28-yard field-goal try in the second quarter before later adding a 38-yard make in the fourth. With Atlanta's bye week in Week 11, Moody's next chance to build on Sunday's performance will come in Week 12 against the Vikings.

short_comment: Hooper recorded an eight-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.
long_comment: Hooper was on the field for just 11 of the Falcons' 72 offensive snaps, with his 15 percent share placing him comfortably behind Kyle Pitts (76 percent) and Charlie Woerner (44 percent) among Atlanta tight ends. The 32-year-old Hooper hasn't played more than half of the snaps in any of Atlanta's first 10 games and has turned in a 10-84-1 receiving line on 12 targets, a level of production that keeps him well off the fantasy radar.

short_comment: Head coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday that London was cleared of a concussion near the end of Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
long_comment: London was checked for a possible concussion in the fourth quarter of Week 10 action, but the result of the evaluation wasn't reported before the game concluded. Prior to his exit Sunday, he posted his third 100-yard game (109, to be exact) of the campaign on six catches and a season-high 12 targets. London will continue to operate as the Falcons' No. 1 WR after a Week 11 bye in the team's next game Sunday, Nov. 29, at Minnesota.

short_comment: Penix completed 23 of 43 passes for 286 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and rushed four times for 29 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.
long_comment: Penix struggled while the game was still in question, but he did manage to pad his stats some down the stretch as the Falcons unsuccessfully tried to overcome their deficit. Penix connected with eight different targets overall on the afternoon, and he ultimately finished with a season high in passing yards. Penix has now tossed six interceptions in the last three games, however, and he'll look to regroup during the Week 11 bye before tackling a difficult matchup against the Vikings on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Pitts brought in four of five targets for 50 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
long_comment: The veteran tight end had a slow start to the day before coming on when the Falcons went especially pass-heavy in the second half. Pitts' fumble, his first of the season, came with just over four minutes remaining in the game after the contest was out of reach, and his catch total was his highest since Week 7. Pitts remains a key complementary option in an Atlanta passing attack that's scuffled of late, and he'll look to bounce back after the Falcons emerge from a Week 11 bye with a Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Robinson rushed 16 times for 71 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for six yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
long_comment: The Falcons were down 14-3 by halftime and 21-3 doing into the final period, so Robinson's opportunities progressively dwindled due to game script. However, the star running back still averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry and recorded his sixth rushing touchdown of the season on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter. Robinson has at least four receptions in three of the last four games, and he'll now have a Week 11 bye to rest up before a tough Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Daniels (Achilles) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
long_comment: Daniels popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to an Achilles injury, but his full session Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's home game. The rookie fourth-rounder has accumulated 61 tackles (41 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Henderson and the Falcons agreed to a two-year contract extension Friday.
long_comment: Per Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network, Henderson's extension is worth up to $20 million and includes $11 million guaranteed. Henderson has started at outside cornerback in each of his last six outings, and he was moved into the starting lineup after A.J. Terrell landed on injured reserve in late September due to a groin injury. Across eight regular-season games, Henderson has logged 41 tackles (32 solo), nine pass defenses, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery.

short_comment: Thomas and the Falcons agreed to a three-year extension worth up to $33 million Friday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
long_comment: The extension means Thomas -- a third-round selection of the Cardinals in the 2022 NFL Draft -- will be under contract with the Falcons through the 2029 season. The fifth-year pro has stepped into a larger role defensively this year due to the absences of James Pearce (back) and Jalon Walker (knee, IR), the former of whom missed the first eight games of the 2026 campaign while serving a suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy. Thomas has accumulated 25 tackles (nine solo), including 2.0 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: The Ravens traded Vorhees and a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick to the Falcons on Tuesday in exchange for Ryan Neuzil, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: The move gives the Falcons additional depth at the guard position behind starters Chris Lindstrom and Matthew Bergeron. Vorhees -- a seventh-round selection of the Ravens in the 2023 NFL Draft -- started in all 17 regular-season games in 2025, but he's started in only two of five contests this year. He also missed two games in October while recovering from a foot injury.

short_comment: Brissett completed 24 of 37 passes for 276 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers. He added seven rushing yards on two carries.
long_comment: It was another decent showing for the veteran quarterback, and his first TD pass in two games as a Raven came on a trick that involved a direct snap to Derrick Henry, who flipped it Brissett for a 52-yard strike to Rashod Bateman. Brissett has also kept Zay Flowers relevant, feeding the wideout 18 targets for a 14-171-0 line. Baltimore's passing attack will try to keep improving in Week 12 against the Texans.

short_comment: Flowers caught eight of 11 targets for 97 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
long_comment: No other Raven caught more than four passes or saw more than six targets as Flowers continues to build chemistry with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett. The fourth-year wideout has posted a 14-171-0 line on 18 targets in Brissett's first two starts for Baltimore, immediately establishing a strong floor. Flowers will try to keep rolling in Week 12 against what has been a surprisingly vulnerable Texans defense.

short_comment: Henry cleared concussion protocol and was made available to the media following Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers, Giana Han of the Baltimore Banner reports.
long_comment: Henry was checked for a concussion in the fourth quarter of the contest, but evidently passed all tests. Prior to his exit, Henry carried 13 times for 94 yards and a touchdown and hauled in four of his five targets for 17 yards. He also lost his second fumble of the season. Henry looks like he'll be ready to handle his normal role as the lead option out of the Baltimore backfield next Sunday against the Texans.

short_comment: Sarratt (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Carolina.
long_comment: Sarratt has been active for two games this season, most recently appearing in Week 4 versus the Titans. Since then, he's been held out. His next opportunity to play will come in Week 12 versus the Texans.

short_comment: Randall (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Carolina.
long_comment: Randall was recently reinstated from injured reserve. However, with Derrick Henry, Justice Hill and Rasheen Ali available versus the Panthers, Randall will be inactive.

short_comment: Slovis (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Panthers but will serve as the Ravens' emergency quarterback.
long_comment: Slovis will be inactive once again. However, if Jacoby Brissett and Joe Fagnano exit Sunday's meeting with Carolina due to an injury, illness or ejection, Slovis will be available to play.

short_comment: The Ravens elevated Vannett from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
long_comment: Vannett will be promoted to the Ravens' 53-man roster for a second consecutive week, and he will be available for Sunday's game against the Panthers. He played 20 snaps (14 on offense, six on special teams) and didn't show up in the box score otherwise during Monday's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.

short_comment: Ioane (shoulder/knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Cordell Woodland of 105.7 The Fan Baltimore reports.
long_comment: The offensive guard was limited during Wednesday's session. Ioane left Monday's loss to the Chargers with a shoulder injury and didn't return. The first-round pick out of Penn State has started all nine games he's played in this season.

short_comment: Ali played all 19 of his snaps on special teams in Monday's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.
long_comment: For the second week in a row, Ali was deployed exclusively on special teams while the Ravens leaned on Derrick Henry and Justice Hill to handle all the snaps out of the backfield. Ali has logged just seven total snaps on offense all season, carrying six times for 24 yards.

short_comment: The Ravens believe "there's a chance" that Jackson (thumb) could return for their Week 16 matchup with the Browns, assuming all goes well in his recovery from right thumb surgery, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. While Jackson remains sidelined for at least a few more weeks, the Ravens will entrust trade-deadline acquisition Jacoby Brissett to direct the offense.

short_comment: Smith finished Monday's Week 10 loss to the Chargers with eight tackles (six solo).
long_comment: Kyle Hamilton led Baltimore with 10 tackles, and Smith was among three players who finished second with eight stops apiece. The veteran linebacker has hit the eight-tackle mark in four straight games and in eight of his 10 contests overall this season. Smith is tied for 11th in the NFL with 82 tackles on the campaign.

short_comment: Hamilton posted 10 tackles (three solo) against the Chargers in Monday's Week 10 loss.
long_comment: Hamilton is managing a hip injury but played all but one of Baltimore's defensive snaps Monday. He led the team with 10 stops, which were the second-most he's recorded in a contest so far this season. Hamilton seems to be on his way to a third consecutive triple-digit tackle campaign, as he has 70 stops through 10 games on the season.

short_comment: Green racked up six tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, in Monday's Week 10 loss to the Chargers.
long_comment: Green's first sack came late in the second quarter, and he brought down Chargers QB Justin Herbert again early in the fourth. After registering 3.5 sacks in 17 regular-season games as a rookie last year, Green has already exceeded that mark with 5.5 sacks through 10 contests this season. His six total tackles in Week 10 also tied his career-high mark.

short_comment: Cuevas caught all three of his targets for 37 yards during Monday night's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.
long_comment: Cuevas had an immediate connection with new starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett, reeling in at least three passes for the second time this season and the first time since Week 6. The tight end ranked fourth at his position with 11 offensive snaps, sitting behind Mark Andrews (40), Matthew Hibner (22) and Nick Vannett (14). Cuevas has now caught 13 of 16 targets for 171 yards and a touchdown over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

short_comment: Patterson went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made both of his PATs during Monday night's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.
long_comment: Patterson was signed by the Ravens on Wednesday, and he was able to make a 26-yard field goal as time expired in the first half before later adding a 36-yard make in the third quarter. With Tyler Loop (groin) set to miss at least two more contests while on injured reserve, Patterson will likely remain the team's starting kicker for the time being.

short_comment: Hill turned three carries into four yards and added five catches on seven targets for 34 yards during the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday.
long_comment: Hill also had a 14-yard carry midway through the first quarter, but the play was nullified by an offensive holding call. The veteran running back connected on a 17-yard catch with Jacoby Brissett late in the third, which set up a 36-yard field goal by Riley Patterson four plays later. Hill's five catches were a season high, and even with the Ravens' quarterback carousel over the last three weeks, the 2019 fourth-rounder has hauled in at least three passes in each of his last five outings. Losers of five straight games, the Ravens will look to turn their fortunes around in a Week 11 road tilt against the Panthers on Sunday.

short_comment: Bateman brought in three of five targets for 42 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
long_comment: Bateman put together a solid performance during his first opportunity to work with Jacoby Brissett, posting his best receiving yardage total since Week 5. The veteran wideout also recorded multiple receptions for the first time in three games, and two of his three catches went for first downs. Bateman seemed to lay a solid foundation with his new signal-caller, and he'll look to continue building on it in a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.

short_comment: Shakir caught five of nine targets for 101 yards while rushing twice for two yards in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
long_comment: Shakir led the Bills in receiving yards in the absence of TE Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle), posting 10 more than DJ Moore, who had one more target than Shakir. Sunday marked Shakir's first time reaching the 100-yard threshold since a 110-yard showing in Week 12 of last season. Shakir will look to build on this outing as he searches for his second TD of the season Thursday against the Chiefs.

short_comment: Moore caught eight of 10 targets for 91 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
long_comment: Moore's four-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter gave him his first multi-game regular-season touchdown streak since Weeks 15 and 16 of the 2025 campaign with the Bears. He briefly left the game later in the first half to have his knee looked at but promptly returned and ultimately reached the 90-yard threshold for a second consecutive game while leading the team in targets. Barring a setback with his knee on a short week, Moore should continue to work as Buffalo's top wide receiver Thanksgiving night against the Chiefs.

short_comment: Cook rushed 22 times for 89 yards and a touchdown while catching two of three targets for three yards in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
long_comment: Cook extended his touchdown streak to nine games with a one-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. He accounted for all but five of Buffalo's rushing attempts as Josh Allen finished without one, but Cook came up short of 100 scrimmage yards for the first time since Week 4. The reigning NFL rushing yards leader continues to put up stellar production heading into Thursday night's home game against the Chiefs.

short_comment: Allen completed 27 of 45 passes for 304 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
long_comment: Allen threw a four-yard touchdown pass to DJ Moore in the second quarter but got picked off twice later in the first half and had a would-be third interception nullified by a penalty on the penultimate play before halftime. Despite some sloppy play and zero rushing production from Allen, the 9-1 Bills cruised past the 1-9 Dolphins as the star QB raised his season total to 25 touchdowns (14 passing, 11 rushing). Buffalo's likely to encounter more resistance Thursday night against the 8-2 Chiefs. Allen is 5-1 against Patrick Mahomes in the regular season but 0-4 when they face off in the playoffs.

short_comment: Hamlin (toe) is active for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
long_comment: Hamlin missed the first two practices of Week 11 prep due to a toe injury, but he earned the questionable tag following Friday's limited session. The sixth-year defensive back was cleared by medical staff to play Sunday following pregame warmups, and he'll provide depth in the secondary behind Amani Hooker and Cole Bishop.

short_comment: Shavers (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
long_comment: Shavers was activated from the reserve/PUP list Saturday, and the San Diego State product has been officially cleared to play Sunday in what will be his first game since the Bills AFC wild-card round win over the Jaguars in January, when he tore his ACL. Shavers will likely operate in a rotational role on offense behind DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman.

short_comment: Sanders (shoulder) is inactive for Sunday's game against Miami.
long_comment: Sanders logged a full practice Wednesday, though he posted limited sessions on Thursday and Friday. After carrying a questionable designation ahead of Sunday's meeting with the Dolphins, he has been ruled out, meaning his next opportunity to get back on the field will come in Week 12 versus the Chiefs.

short_comment: Oliver (oblique) is active for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
long_comment: Oliver popped up on the injury report after informing the team's medical staff of oblique pain and was listed as questionable. However, the veteran is cleared to play for Sunday's divisional meeting with Miami, potentially resulting in fewer snaps for DeWayne Carter, Greg Gaines and Landon Jackson.

short_comment: Hawes (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
long_comment: Hawes was in danger of missing this contest due to a shoulder issue, though he will avoid his first absence of the 2026 campaign Sunday versus Miami. With Dalton Kincaid (thumb) sidelined in Week 11, Hawes will have an opportunity to get more involved than usual behind Dawson Knox.

short_comment: Bell (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
long_comment: Bell made his third appearance of the 2026 campaign in Week 10, though he went without a catch. With Tyrell Shavers (knee) cleared to play for Sunday's divisional clash with Miami after spending time on injured reserve, Bell's services won't be needed. His next opportunity to play will come in Week 12 against the Chiefs.

short_comment: Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
long_comment: Listed as doubtful heading into the weekend after failing to practice in any capacity Wednesday through Friday, Kincaid will wind up missing his first game of the season. Kincaid's 4.5 targets per game will be filtered out among the Bills' other pass-catching options, including Dawson Knox, who will operate as the team's clear No. 1 tight end this week. The Bills will face a quick turnaround for Week 12 with a Thursday matchup versus the Chiefs, so Kincaid may need to practice in some fashion prior to that contest to put himself on a path to play.

short_comment: Alford (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
long_comment: Alford upgraded his practice participation in each subsequent session of Week 11 prep as he progressed through the five stages of the NFL's concussion protocol. The slot cornerback has been cleared by an independent neurologist and is all set to suit up for Sunday's game.

short_comment: Knox will likely be the Bills' top tight end against the Dolphins on Sunday, given that Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is listed as doubtful for that contest, Maddy Glab of the Bills' official site reports.
long_comment: Kincaid was held out of practice all week while tending to thumb and ankle injuries, and he's trending toward being inactive for Sunday's AFC East tilt. If Kincaid is indeed ruled out, then Knox will operate as the Bills' top tight end, with Jackson Hawes (shoulder) and Keleki Latu also in line for larger roles on offense. Knox has 14 catches (on 20 targets) for 86 yards and a touchdown through nine regular-season games, and the Bills face a Dolphins defense that ranks 25th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to opposing tight ends.

short_comment: Hooker (knee) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
long_comment: Hooker was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday due to a knee injury, but the veteran safety was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's AFC East showdown. Hooker made his Bills debut against the Jets in Week 10, when he logged seven tackles (four solo) and one pass defense in a 31-12 win for Buffalo.

short_comment: Davis (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
long_comment: The backup running back was managed during the practice week but is good to go for his normal role behind lead back James Cook. With the Bills listed as 16.5-point favorites, Davis could see some extra reps in garbage time if Buffalo does indeed blow out Miami.

short_comment: Bishop (knee) was a full participant in practice Thursday, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.
long_comment: The safety was limited during Wednesday's session. Bishop has yet to miss a game this season, and it doesn't appear that streak will be snapped Sunday. He has 54 tackles (32 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass breakups and a forced fumble in 2026.

short_comment: Parker accumulated five tackles (three solo), including 2.0 sacks, in the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
long_comment: Parker sacked his former Clemson quarterback Cade Klubnik twice in the Bills' blowout win. The rookie second-rounder called his shot, discussing his wishes to sack Klubnik while answering a question from Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo in late April.

short_comment: Johnson caught his only target for four yards in a 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
long_comment: For the third time in seven appearances this season, Johnson didn't log a single carry. The veteran running back also didn't have much of a role in the passing game with just one target. In fact, Johnson tallied just 10 offensive snaps, finishing behind both starter James Cook (35) and fellow backup Ray Davis (12). Johnson has had a few productive performances as a pass catcher this season, but his role is too unpredictable to warrant weekly fantasy consideration.

short_comment: The Bills placed Reed-Adams (back) on injured reserve Tuesday.
long_comment: It's not immediately clear when he suffered the back injury, but Reed-Adams will now have to sit out at least four games as he recovers. His absence leaves veteran Austin Corbett as Buffalo's undisputed backup plan at guard behind starters Alec Anderson and O'Cyrus Torrence.

short_comment: Bass made his sole field-goal attempt and all four PATs in the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
long_comment: Bass made a 37-yard field goal in the second quarter of Sunday's contest. The kicker continues his perfect streak, having made all 20 of his field-goal attempts so far in 2026, with three such conversions coming from beyond 50 yards.

short_comment: Coleman caught one of three targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
long_comment: Coleman failed to reel in multiple passes for the third time in the team's last five contests, and he played just 52 percent of the team's offensive snaps in the contest, his lowest percentage since Week 1. The wide receiver was briefly sidelined while being evaluated for a head injury before returning to the contest, which likely contributed to his lower workload. Coleman will continue to be an unpredictable fantasy option in Week 11 versus the Dolphins.

short_comment: Coker entered the league's concussion protocol following Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens, Sheena Quick of Fox Sports Radio 1340 reports.
long_comment: Coker was shaken up at the end of a six-yard catch late in the fourth quarter on what appeared to be a helmet-to-helmet hit. He'll have to progress through league's concussion protocol over the next few days, and his status for Week 12 against the Buccaneers on Monday, Nov. 30, is up in the air. He finished Sunday's game with four catches (on seven targets) for 47 yards, and that workload would be absorbed by John Metchie, Brycen Tremayne and Xavier Legette if Coker cannot play against Tampa Bay.

short_comment: Jackson (groin) is active for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Jackson was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday and has practiced in full since then. He was listed as questionable to suit up versus Baltimore, though he is now cleared to play for the first time since Week 3.

short_comment: Sanders (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Baltimore, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Sanders has appeared in just one game this season, which was in Week 9 versus Denver. With Darren Waller (knee) and Tommy Tremble (knee) both active, Sanders will now miss his second consecutive contest. His next opportunity to play will come in Week 12 versus Tampa Bay.

short_comment: King (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Ravens on Sunday, Steve Reed of the Associated Press reports.
long_comment: King will only play Sunday if both Bryce Young and Kenny Pickett leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

short_comment: Tremble (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
long_comment: Tremble opened Week 11 prep as a non-participant Wednesday due to a knee injury, which he followed up with limited sessions Thursday and Friday and a questionable tag for Sunday. The same can be said for fellow TE Darren Waller (knee), and both now are available to the Panthers offense. In nine outings this season, Tremble has compiled a 25-227-3 line on 35 targets.

short_comment: Waller (knee) is listed as active Sunday against the Ravens, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
long_comment: The Panthers kicked off Week 11 prep with their top two tight ends (Waller and Tommy Tremble) not practicing due to knee injuries, after which head coach Dave Canales told Steve Reed of the Associated Press that those issues were a "concern." Both Waller and Tremble were limited Thursday and Friday and entered the weekend listed as questionable. Now that Waller is confirmed to be active -- along with Tremble -- the former will look to continue to build upon his 25-323-4 line on 39 targets that he's accrued in nine appearances this season.

short_comment: Christensen (hamstring) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
long_comment: The offensive lineman had his 21-day practice window opened 18 days ago, so a decision will need to be made one way or another on activating him from injured reserve next week. Christensen hasn't played in a game this season.

short_comment: The Panthers placed Simmons (knee) on injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Simmons will be required to miss at least the next four games for Carolina. He's logged just six defensive snaps this season and another 206 on special teams.

short_comment: Brooks (groin) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
long_comment: Brooks was a full practice participant in all three sessions during Week 11 prep. However, the third-year running back is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve, and he's slated to miss his eighth consecutive game while recovering from a groin injury. Trevor Etienne, Anthony Tyus and AJ Dillon will continue to operate as the Panthers' backfield depth options behind Chuba Hubbard in the absence of Brooks, whose next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Buccaneers on Monday, Nov. 30.

short_comment: Lee (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
long_comment: Lee missed the Panthers' last two games due to a hamstring injury. However, his full participation in Wednesday's practice indicates that the rookie fourth-rounder has fully recovered from his injury, and Lee should be back on the field for the Panthers against the Ravens on Sunday.

short_comment: Young was listed with a sore foot on Wednesday's injury report but was a full participant in the Panthers' first Week 11 practice.
long_comment: Per Steve Reed of the Associated Press, head coach Dave Canales said that Young experienced some soreness in his foot coming out of Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. However, after receiving treatment over the last couple of days, Young responded well enough to take every rep in practice to kick off Week 11 prep. The signal-caller isn't expected to face any limitations during this Sunday's matchup with the Ravens.

short_comment: Dodson logged seven tackles (two solo) Sunday in a 20-17 win over New Orleans.
long_comment: Dodson finished second on the Panthers in stops behind Devin Lloyd (nine). It was the second straight start for Dodson as a result of Bobby Okereke being sidelined by a foot injury. If Okereke can't return for this Sunday's matchup against Baltimore, Dodson would figure to start and handle an every-down role again.

short_comment: Lloyd registered nine tackles (five solo) and an interception in Sunday's 20-17 win over New Orleans.
long_comment: Lloyd was prolific as a tackler, leading Carolina with nine stops. He also put an end to the Saints' first offensive possession of the game with an interception of Tyler Shough. The pickoff was Lloyd's third of the campaign, a tally he's now reached in three of his five NFL seasons. With 63 tackles through eight contests, Lloyd is also on pace to reach triple-digit tackles for the fourth time.

short_comment: Legette didn't produce any output in the boxscore during Carolina's win over the Saints on Sunday.
long_comment: Legette made his return to the lineup after having been sidelined since Week 2 due to a knee injury, but he ended up playing just two snaps on offense. He will look to be more involved during next week's matchup versus the Ravens.

short_comment: Metchie caught his only target for four yards Sunday in a 20-17 win against New Orleans.
long_comment: Metchie's only catch and target came late in the third quarter, as he logged four yards on a third-down play to help set up a Ryan Fitzgerald field goal. The veteran wideout had a streak of six games with multiple catches snapped in the Carolina victory. Metchie finished third among Panthers wideouts with 23 offensive snaps, and he's produced like a No. 3 receiver this year, logging no more than three catches and 40 yards in any of his eight games to date.

short_comment: Etienne took three carries for one yard and caught both of his two targets for nine yards during Sunday's 20-17 win at New Orleans. He also returned three punts for 43 yards.
long_comment: Etienne again played second fiddle to starter Chuba Hubbard in Week 10 with Jonathon Brooks sidelined by a groin injury, and Etienne got his second-most touches of the season. His role on offense in Week 11 will depend on Brooks' status, but the vast majority of the Panthers' snaps at tailback will continue to go to Hubbard.

short_comment: Fitzgerald made two of his three field-goal attempts and both PATs in the Panthers' 20-17 win over the Saints on Sunday.
long_comment: Fitzgerald's 54-yard field goal as time expired iced the game for the Panthers. The kicker made another field goal from 55 yards while also missing his first attempt of the night from 48 yards out. Fitzgerald moves to 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts and 18-for-23 on PATs so far during the 2026 regular season.

short_comment: McMillan caught three of seven targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over New Orleans.
long_comment: The seven targets led the Panthers on the afternoon, but the second-year wideout wasn't able to do much with them. The 35 yards were McMillan's lowest total since Week 3, and he'll take a 49-660-3 line on 78 targets through nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Ravens.

short_comment: Hubbard carried the ball 27 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns and caught all five of his targets for 80 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints.
long_comment: The 27-year-old RB kept the Panthers' offense afloat nearly single-handedly, as he set a new career high with 172 scrimmage yards while scoring both the team's TDs, on a two-yard run in the first quarter and a one-yard plunge in the fourth. Hubbard's 80 receiving yards were easily a new career high, topping the 3-57-0 line on three targets he recorded in Week 15 of the 2022 season against the Steelers. Over Hubbard's last six games, he surged to 697 scrimmage yards and six rushing touchdowns, and he'll look keep rolling in a Week 11 clash with the Ravens.

short_comment: Phillips (hamstring) is active against the Saints on Sunday, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
long_comment: Phillips has been cleared by medical staff to return from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Prior to the injury, he accumulated 10 tackles (three solo), including 2.5 sacks, across five regular-season games. His return will bolster the Panthers' pass rush alongside Patrick Jones, Trevis Gipson and Princely Umanmielen.

short_comment: Loveland caught all three of his targets for 29 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.
long_comment: While he didn't get much target volume, Loveland was still able to make an impact with a 15-yard TD reception in the second quarter that saw him hurdle a defender without even breaking stride on his way to the end zone. It was the tight end's third score of the season, all of which have come during Chicago's current five-game win streak, and after a slow start to the season Loveland has delivered a 27-282-3 line on 37 targets during that period. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 12 against the Lions.

short_comment: Odunze caught all four of his targets for 45 yards in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.
long_comment: The four grabs led the Bears on the afternoon, as the offense looked a little sluggish coming out of its bye. Odunze's longest gain went for just 19 yards, and rookie Zavion Thomas wound up leading the team in receiving yards thanks to a 40-yard connection with Caleb Williams in the third quarter. Odunze has caught exactly four passes in four straight games, a stretch in which he's produced a 16-261-1 line on 22 targets. The third-year wideout will try to get more involved in a potential Week 12 barn burner against the Lions.

short_comment: Burden caught two of three targets for 10 yards and added three yards on his only carry in Sunday's 21-13 win over New Orleans.
long_comment: It was the worst performance of the season for Burden, who suffered a concussion in the Bears' last game in Week 9 but used a bye week to clear the protocol and avoid missing any additional time. The second-year wideout saw his three-game scoring streak come to an end, and on the season he sports a 51-654-4 line on 69 targets through 10 contests. Burden will look to bounce back in a potential Week 12 barn burner against the Lions.

short_comment: Williams completed 15 of 23 passes for 181 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints. He added 11 rushing yards on four carries.
long_comment: The Bears' offense looked a little sluggish coming out of its bye, and both of Williams' TD passes came in the second quarter as he connected with D'Andre Swift on a three-yard shovel pass and Colston Loveland on a 15-yard score. Williams failed to reach 200 passing yards for the first time since Week 2, and he'll take a somewhat disappointing 10:6 TD:INT thorough seven games into a Week 12 clash with the Lions.

short_comment: Monangai carried the ball eight times for 18 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.
long_comment: Making his return from a five-game absence due to turf toe, Monangai wasn't able to generate much offense, as D'Andre Swift led the backfield with 15 touches and 59 scrimmage yards, plus a short receiving TD. Surprisingly, Salvon Ahmed also handled six carries, all in the fourth quarter when the game seemed well in hand. Monangai should see his usage increase as he puts the injury further behind him, and a late lost fumble by Swift -- his third of the season, a new career high -- might encourage coach Ben Johnson to prioritize Monangai even more in Week 12 against the Lions.

short_comment: Swift carried the ball 13 times for 51 yards and caught both his targets for eight yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.
long_comment: The Bears' offense looked a little sluggish coming out of its bye, and Swift wound up leading the backfield in scrimmage yards on the afternoon, highlighting his performance with a three-yard TD pass from Caleb Williams in the second quarter. Swift's 15 touches also led the backfield, as a returning Kyle Monangai got eased back into action with eight touches. Surprisingly, Salvon Ahmed also handled six carries, all in the fourth quarter when the game seemed well in hand. Swift did lose his third fumble of the season, a new career high, but the TD was his 11th of the year, also a new personal best. Monangai could see his workload increase as he puts his turf toe injury further behind him, but Swift seems to have a firm hold of the No. 1 job heading into a Week 12 clash with the team that drafted him in 2020, the Lions.

short_comment: Johnson (ankle) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Saints, Courtney Cronin of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Johnson injured his ankle while on kickoff coverage early in the first quarter. He was carted off the field, and medical staff have determined that the injury is severe enough for Johnson to be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. Salvon Ahmed will move into the RB3 role behind D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai in Johnson's absence.

short_comment: Keenum (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as Chicago's emergency third quarterback Sunday versus the Saints.
long_comment: It's the fifth straight week that Keenum will work as the Bears' emergency third quarterback. That means he can enter Sunday's contest only if both Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent have to exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

short_comment: Thomas (ankle) is active for Sunday's matchup against New Orleans.
long_comment: Thomas popped up on the practice report as a nonparticipant Friday due to an ankle issue and was initially deemed questionable for Sunday. However, the rookie will ultimately be able to play through the issue. Thomas typically has a minimal role on offense, as he's caught more than one pass in only one of his nine appearances so far. However, he's worked as Chicago's primary kickoff returner and should again contribute in that role against the Saints.
