short_comment: The Bears elevated Ahmed from the practice squad Saturday.
long_comment: Even with Kyle Monangai (toe) back from his toe injury for Sunday's game against New Orleans, Ahmed is up as the Bears' fourth running back, though he could be active ahead of Roschon Johnson, who played behind Ahmed in Week 9 against the Bucs.

short_comment: Simmons has no injury designation ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Saints.
long_comment: Simmons logged full participation in Friday's practice after beginning the week as limited with a knee injury. Since joining the Bears, the 29-year-old has 10 tackles (six solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass breakups on 119 defensive snaps.

short_comment: Stevenson (hand) was not listed on the Bears' estimated injury report Wednesday.
long_comment: Stevenson injured his hand during the Bears' Week 9 win over the Buccaneers. He had additional time to rest thanks to the Week 10 bye, and given Stevenson's absence from Wednesday's estimated practice report, the fourth-year defensive back should suit up Sunday against the Saints. He has accumulated 34 tackles (23 solo) and four pass defenses through eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Johnson recorded three tackles (one solo) and a pick-six during the Bears' 27-24 win over the Buccaneers in Week 9.
long_comment: In a game that featured seven turnovers between the two teams, Johnson's takeaway was arguably the most impactful of them all. He jumped in front of a Baker Mayfield pass intended for Cade Otton late in the third quarter, which Johnson returned 67 yards to the house for the second pick-six of his NFL career. The veteran defensive back is up to 27 tackles (21 solo), three pass defenses (including a pick-six) and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Lewis produced six tackles (three solo) and one interception during the Bears' 27-24 win over the Buccaneers in Week 9.
long_comment: Lewis jumped in front of a Baker Mayfield pass intended for Tez Johnson late in the second quarter, although the Bears offense turned the ball over on the very next play. It was the first interception of the season for Lewis and second of his career. The veteran safety is up to 35 tackles (25 solo) and two pass defenses across eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Roush caught both of his two targets for 23 yards during Sunday's 27-24 win versus the Buccaneers.
long_comment: Roush, who has been utilized heavily as a blocker through nine games, achieved a new career high in receiving yards in Week 9. Roush has been relatively efficient with his limited targets so far this season, but Colston Loveland should be expected to continue to handle a substantial majority of the Bears' pass-catching duties at tight end as long as he's available.

short_comment: Raymond caught four passes for 32 yards on seven targets in Sunday night's 27-24 win over the Bucs.
long_comment: Raymond tied Rome Odunze for second on the team in targets behind Luther Burden (nine), but Burden was injured late in the fourth quarter. If he needs to miss any time, Raymond projects to see elevated snaps alongside Odunze and Colston Loveland. The good news for Burden is he'll have two weeks to heal up with the Bears headed into their bye in Week 10.

short_comment: Santos made both of his two field-goal attempts and converted all three of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 27-24 win versus the Buccaneers.
long_comment: It was an up-and-down night for Chicago's offense Sunday, as it moved the ball relatively well but committed five turnovers. Nevertheless, Santos got an opportunity to win the game on the last play of regulation with a 38-yard field goal, and it looked good from the moment it left his foot. Following a bye in Week 10, the Bears will play host to the Saints in Week 11, at which point fantasy managers might want to confirm the weather forecast in Chicago before locking Santos back into their lineups.

short_comment: Jarrett (groin) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Buccaneers.
long_comment: After missing the Bears' walk-through practice Wednesday, Jarrett logged a limited practice Thursday and then upgraded again to a full practice Friday. He should start on the interior of the defensive line next to Jeffery Simmons again in Week 9.

short_comment: Dugger (quadriceps) is questionable for Monday night's game against the Commanders.
long_comment: Dugger has missed the past three games, but he has a chance to get back on the field against Washington. The veteran safety has appeared in just four games this season, logging 10 tackles (five solo) and a pass breakup.

short_comment: Risner (knees) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Commanders, Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com reports.
long_comment: Risner was held out of practice all week due to injuries to both of his knees that he sustained in Week 10 against the Steelers. Jalen Rivers figures to start at right guard Monday in the absence of Risner, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Hill (illness) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Commanders.
long_comment: Hill was held out of practice all week while battling through an illness. He could still suit up Monday if he progresses enough in his recovery, but if he's not cleared to play, then Josh Newton, PJ Jules and DJ Ivey would all be in line for more snaps in the secondary.

short_comment: Iosivas (thumb) is listed as doubtful for Monday's game against the Commanders.
long_comment: Iosivas was a full participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep, but it looks like the fourth-year wide receiver will stay on injured reserve for at least one more week while recovering from a thumb injury. If he's inactive for Monday's game, then his next chance to play would be Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Burrow (illness) does not have an injury designation ahead of Monday's game against the Commanders.
long_comment: Burrow dealt with an illness during Week 11 prep, but with no injury tag the 2020 first overall pick has been officially cleared to play Monday night -- and per ESPN.com he is confident he will do so at "full strength." He's thrown at least three touchdowns in each of his last five outings, and over that span he has completed 77.6 percent of his passes for 1,624 yards, 20 touchdowns and three interceptions while turning 13 carries into 47 yards and two scores. The Bengals will face a Commanders defense that ranks 31st in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (244.8) and 30th in red-zone touchdown rate (71.9 percent).

short_comment: The Bengals placed Burks (groin) on injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Burks has been working through a groin issue for the past couple of weeks, and he aggravated the injury during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. His placement on IR means he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 20.

short_comment: Hinton (illness) was a full participant in practice Thursday, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: The offensive tackle came down with the illness last Sunday morning and had to miss the Bengals' win over the Steelers that night. Hinton seems to be over the illness, and he should be ready to resume his role as a reserve lineman Monday night against the Commanders.

short_comment: The Bengals designated Bozeman (forearm) for return from injured reserve Thursday.
long_comment: The linebacker suffered a broken forearm in Week 5 against the Dolphins but now has a maximum of 21 days to get ready for a return to action. He played just one defensive snap across the first four games of the season but was a fixture on special teams.

short_comment: Higgins (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: It's a new "injury" for Higgins, but the full participation level suggests it's nothing serious after the wideout was managed late in last Sunday night's blowout win over the Steelers, per Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer. Higgins already has a fantasy-friendly 53 catches (on 73 targets) for 824 yards and six touchdowns through nine games. He's on pace for a career year in 2026.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Flacco took the field for the Bengals' final possession of Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers, attempting no passes while handing off to running back Tahj Brooks on all three of his snaps.
long_comment: With the Bengals having built their lead to 20 by the midway point of the fourth quarter, head coach Zac Taylor pulled starter Joe Burrow from the contest and turned to Flacco to run down the clock in the win. The appearance was Flacco's third of the season, but the veteran signal-caller still has yet to attempt a pass.

short_comment: Battle finished Sunday's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh with six tackles (four solo), one defensed pass and one forced fumble.
long_comment: Battle ranked second on Cincinnati in stops. One of his six tackles went for a loss, and the 25-year-old also forced a fumble, though it was recovered by the Steelers. Battle has played every defensive snap in seven of the Bengals' nine contests this season, and he's collected 58 tackles and eight defensed passes, including three interceptions.

short_comment: Knight finished with eight tackles (six solo) and a defensed pass against the Steelers in a 38-18 victory Sunday.
long_comment: Knight led Cincinnati in tackles in the blowout win. The second-year linebacker has recorded exactly eight stops in four of his past five games, and he's finished with at least that tally in all but three of his appearances overall this season. Knight hasn't yet recorded a sack, but he's on pace to blow by his rookie total of 106 stops, as he has 71 tackles across nine games.

short_comment: Carter posted six tackles (two solo) and a defensed pass in Sunday's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh.
long_comment: Carter's tackle tally tied for second-most on the Bengals. The second-year pro has now reached the six-tackle mark in all but one of his nine games this season. Carter leads the Bengals with 74 stops overall, and he's recorded 1.5 sacks, five defensed passes (including an interception) and two forced fumbles.

short_comment: Sample caught all three of his targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-18 win against Pittsburgh.
long_comment: Sample entered the contest with no catches over his previous two games, but he tied season-high marks in both receptions and targets versus the Steelers. He gave Cincinnati a two-score lead just after the beginning of the second quarter when he hauled in a three-yard TD from Joe Burrow. Sample has two touchdowns over his past four games, but with just five catches for 39 yards during that span, he's almost entirely dependent on getting into the end zone to generate useful fantasy production.

short_comment: McPherson made one of his two field-goal attempts and all five PATs in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday.
long_comment: McPherson converted a 24-yard field-goal attempt on the first drive of the game. The kicker proceeded to miss a 43-yarder in the second quarter of the contest, though the miss did not end up mattering to the final result of the game. McPherson is now 13-for-14 on field-goal attempts and 33-for-33 on PATs over nine contests this season.

short_comment: Meyers caught both of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown while also adding 58 yards as a kick returner during Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers.
long_comment: Meyers reeled in multiple passes for the third straight game, and he was able to secure his first score of the year in the second quarter on a 15-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow. The 26-year-old's 28 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Cincinnati behind Ja'Marr Chase (59), Tee Higgins (51) and Colbie Young (29). With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) nearing a return to action, Meyers may see a sharp drop in offensive opportunities in the near future.

short_comment: Perine turned six carries into 14 yards and a touchdown and hauled in all four of his targets for 25 yards during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday.
long_comment: It looked like Chase Brown found the end zone in the fourth quarter for his third score of the game, but replay assist revealed that his knee came down just short of the goal line. Perine came in on the next play and took the ball for a one-yard touchdown to extend the Bengals' lead to 38-10 following Evan MacPherson's successful extra-point try. It was Perine's third touchdown of the season and first since Week 7 against the Ravens, and over his last five games, he has turned 39 carries into 151 yards (3.9 YPC) and two touchdowns while adding seven catches on as many targets for 44 yards and a score. He'll continue to operate as the Bengals' RB2 behind Brown heading into Week 11 against the Commanders on Monday, Nov. 23.

short_comment: Brooks carried three times for 12 yards while taking the field for three of the Bengals' 66 offensive snaps in Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers.
long_comment: All three of Brooks' carries came during the Bengals' final possession of the fourth quarter, when the team had already built a sizable lead and opted to rest multiple key players, including top running back Chase Brown. Brooks has been active for all nine of the Bengals' games to date but has logged just six carries, all of which have come late in blowout victories. So long as Brown and Samaje Perine are both available, Brooks will continue to see limited playing time on offense.

short_comment: Gesicki caught one pass for nine yards in Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers.
long_comment: Gesicki caught six touchdowns in the first seven games of the season, but he's now produced just three grabs for 20 scoreless yards over the past two contests. The fluky touchdown rate was never going to hold up, and Joe Burrow funnels so many of his targets through Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown that there isn't a whole lot more to go around to Cincinnati's ancillary weapons. Gesicki is a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option most weeks despite running a bunch of routes as the de facto slot receiver.

short_comment: Brown rushed 10 times for 44 yards and brought in eight of nine targets for 39 yards for two touchdowns in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday.
long_comment: Brown averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry, but as is customary, his rushing opportunities were capped in a Bengals offense that typically takes a pass-heavy approach irrespective of game script. He still benefited from that philosophy, however, as he tied his second-highest reception total on the season while ending his seven-game touchdown drought by hitting paydirt twice. Brown will get another favorable opportunity to build on his production in Week 11, when the Bengals travel to D.C. for a matchup with the Commanders.

short_comment: Chase brought in 11 of 14 targets for 231 yards in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday night. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Cincinnati.
long_comment: Chase posted one of his signature 200-yard performances, with Sunday night's qualifying as the fourth of his storied career and marking his third instance accomplishing it against an AFC North rival. Needless to say, all three components of Chase's receiving line led the Bengals by a wide margin on the night as well, and after failing to hit the century mark in yardage in any of the first six games of the season, the star wideout has recorded at least 141 receiving yards in three straight. Chase is now up to a 64-878-7 line on 87 targets across nine games heading into a Week 11 Monday night home road matchup against the Commanders on Nov. 23.

short_comment: Turner (ankle) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
long_comment: Turner was able to play through his ankle injury in Week 9 against the Falcons, and it now looks like it's behind him entirely. He projects to start at cornerback against a pass-heavy Steelers offense Sunday.

short_comment: Campbell logged five tackles (one solo) and three passes defensed, including one interception, in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Campbell's three defended passes matched his season total heading into the contest. The cornerback's biggest moment of the day was intercepting C.J. Stroud at the Cleveland 24-yard line with 48 seconds left in the first half. Campbell's turnover likely stole at least three points from the Texans in a game that was decided by the same swing.

short_comment: Schwesinger logged 13 tackles (eight solo) in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Schwesinger continues to be a model of consistency, having played all 658 defensive snaps for the Browns in 2026. The middle linebacker has logged double-digit tackles in six of the team's 10 contests so far, adding 3.0 sacks and three forced fumbles over that span.

short_comment: Corley caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in addition to returning two kicks for 51 yards during Cleveland's win over the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Corley had not caught a pass across the first nine games of the campaign before hauling in three passes during Sunday's victory. He ended up finishing the contest third on the team in receiving yards behind Harold Fannin and Jerry Jeudy.

short_comment: Wallace caught both of his two targets for nine yards during Sunday's 27-24 win versus the Texans. He also recorded one tackle in kick coverage.
long_comment: Wallace again played a rotational role in Week 10, logging 13 snaps at wide receiver. He was able to draw a season-high two targets and come down with both of them, making him one of eight Browns to catch a pass from quarterback Deshaun Watson Sunday. Barring an injury to one of the wideouts ahead of him on the depth chart, he doesn't have a clear path to more consistent playing time following Cleveland's bye in Week 11.

short_comment: out
long_comment: out

short_comment: Szmyt made two of his three field-goal attempts and all three of his PATs in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Szmyt knocked through field goals from 49 and 26 yards in Sunday's contest. The kicker stumbled in the fourth quarter, missing a 54-yard attempt with 11:02 remaining that would've brought the game within a point. Szmyt is now 21-for-24 on field-goal attempts and 15-for-16 on PATs over 10 regular-season contests in 2026.

short_comment: McLaughlin was limited to one snap on offense and none on special teams in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans.
long_comment: Since Week 7, McLaughlin has logged just three snaps on offense in the Browns' ensuing three games, but prior to Sunday, he still appeared to be in the mix for work on kickoff returns. However, Isaiah Bond and Malachi Corley have since taken over as the team's preferred kickoff returners, leaving McLaughlin without a role on special teams. McLaughlin will likely continue to see little use as Cleveland's No. 3 back behind Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson.

short_comment: Sampson rushed four times for six yards and caught four of six targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans.
long_comment: Sampson hardly carries the ball for Cleveland and is merely the pass-catching complement to Quinshon Judkins out of the backfield. Across five games this season, Sampson has rushed 19 times for 79  yards while adding 16 catches for 152 yards on 22 targets. He's playable in PPR fantasy leagues as a desperation RB2 option, particularly in games for which the Browns are projected to play from behind.

short_comment: Jeudy recorded two catches on four targets for 74 yards in a 27-24 victory over the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Jeudy boosted his final line considerably on a 65-yard connection with Deshaun Watson in the second period. Watson carried the ball into the end zone on the following snap to bring the Browns to within seven points. Jeudy's 74 receiving yards were a season-high mark, though he finished with two or fewer receptions for the third straight week. The veteran wideout is behind both WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, not to mention tight end Harold Fannin, in the pass-catcher pecking order, so he may need to rely on big plays to have a chance to make an impact for fantasy managers.

short_comment: Concepcion caught three of eight targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over Houston. He also gained six yards on one carry.
long_comment: Concepcion finished second on the Browns in targets behind tight end Harold Fannin, who had nine. However, whereas Fannin was able to turn his looks into seven receptions and 91 yards, Concepcion posted a much more modest 3-21-0 line. The rookie wideout departed to the medical tent during the first half of the game due to an undisclosed issue, but he was able to quickly return. Concepcion hasn't put up prolific numbers this season, but he does have at least three receptions in eight of his 10 appearances. Cleveland is on bye in Week 11, so Concepcion will next suit up Sunday, Nov. 29, against Las Vegas.

short_comment: Boston caught just one pass for 16 yards on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans.
long_comment: The rookie wideout entered play Sunday dealing with a toe injury and appeared to aggravate it versus Houston. At less than 100 percent health, Boston was unproductive in the box score and saw a microscopic five percent target share. After popping back up for 6-98-0 receiving last Sunday in New Orleans with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback, Boston reverted to his sluggish ways with Deshaun Watson in Week 10. Over his last four games with Watson, Boston has compiled 11 catches for 95 empty yards. Boston can't be trusted in fantasy lineups until he shows more consistency.

short_comment: Watson completed 25 of 40 passes for 312 yards with no touchdowns and one interception while adding eight rushes for 49 yards and a score in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that remained with Cleveland.
long_comment: Watson helped the Browns overcome a 17-point first-half deficit, even though he didn't throw any touchdown passes for the fourth straight game. The veteran signal-caller did pile up the passing yardage against his old team, however, eclipsing 300 yards for the third straight game in the process. Watson also hit Harold Fannin with a critical 30-yard pass on his last pass attempt of the afternoon to set up Quinshon Judkins' game-winning rushing touchdown, and he'll next draw a highly favorable matchup against the Raiders in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29, following a Week 11 bye.

short_comment: Fannin brought in seven of nine targets for 91 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Fannin led the Browns across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his 30-yard grab on Cleveland's penultimate possession set up Quinshon Judkins' game-winning five-yard touchdown rush on the next play. Fannin's chemistry with Deshaun Watson has been outstanding, and the second-year tight end now has at least 91 receiving yards in three of the past four games. Fannin will remain a central figure in Cleveland's impressive air attack when the team returns to action in a home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 29, following a Week 11 bye.

short_comment: Judkins rushed 10 times for 38 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of five targets for 33 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Judkins' rushing volume was at a season-low level, but the second-year back managed to record his fourth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a five-yard run with just under a minute remaining. That proved to be the game-winning score, and Judkins also mustered his second-highest receiving yardage tally of the campaign. The 2025 first-round pick is averaging just 3.4 yards per carry, however, so he remains far from efficient heading into a Week 11 bye ahead of a Week 12 home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Barnett (hamstring) has returned to Sunday's game against Houston, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
long_comment: Barnett left in the first quarter due to a hamstring injury, but the veteran defensive lineman was cleared by medical staff to return to Sunday's contest.

short_comment: The Browns placed Burton (calf) on injured reserve Saturday, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
long_comment: Burton was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans due to a calf injury that he picked up against the Saints in Week 9. The injury is severe enough for him to warrant an extended absence, and since he's now on IR, Burton will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against the Giants on Sunday, Dec. 20. Since the Browns do not have another fullback on the 53-man roster, the team will likely turn to tight ends Carsen Ryan, Zaire Mitchell-Paden and Blake Whiteheart to provide blocking out of the backfield, per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com.

short_comment: Williams (hamstring) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against Houston.
long_comment: Williams has had his practice reps over the last couple of weeks limited while tending to a hamstring injury, but he has yet to miss a regular-season game, and that trend will continue for Sunday's home tilt. The veteran linebacker has accumulated 62 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, three pass defenses and four forced fumbles through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Ward (quadriceps) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Texans.
long_comment: Ward was managing a quad injury during all of Week 10 prep, but he avoided an injury tag for Sunday's game despite not logging a full practice. The veteran defensive back has 34 tackles (19 solo), nine pass defenses (including three interceptions) and two forced fumbles through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Williams rushed 18 times for 67 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for 24 yards and another score in the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday.
long_comment: Williams continued his highly fantasy-friendly season with his third multi-touchdown showing of the season. The veteran back first struck from one yard out to cap off the opening possession of the game, and he added his second scoring grab of 2026 on an 11-yard catch early in the third quarter. Williams has over 60 rushing yards in three straight games, and he's up to 10 rush TDs, his second consecutive double-digit tally, heading into Thursday's home divisional Thanksgiving clash with the Eagles.

short_comment: Pickens secured seven of 10 targets for 102 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday.
long_comment: Pickens played second fiddle to CeeDee Lamb (11-132-1) in Sunday's blowout win, but that still equated to a rewarding effort for the franchise-tagged receiver. The game marked Pickens' third 100-yard effort of the season and second straight, and he now has seen double-digit targets in four of the last six games overall. Pickens rounded out his day Sunday with his sixth touchdown reception of the campaign on a 10-yard catch in the latter portion of the second quarter, and he should be teed up for another busy day when the Cowboys host the Eagles for a Week 12 matchup on Thanksgiving Day.

short_comment: Lamb brought 11 of 12 targets for 132 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday.
long_comment: Lamb's near-perfect day included his fifth 100-yard effort of the season -- including his second in the last three games -- and his ninth touchdown grab, which came from eight yards out early in the second quarter. Lamb had six double-digit-yardage catches overall on the afternoon, including his game-long 29-yard grab in the first half. Lamb crossed the 1,000-yard mark for the sixth consecutive season in the process, and he'll take an 88-1,108-9 line into a Week 12 Thanksgiving Day clash at home against the Eagles.

short_comment: Prescott completed 28 of 33 passes for 325 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions and added four carries for nine yards and another score in the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday.
long_comment: As the final score and Prescott's numbers indicate, the prolific passer was clicking on all cylinders right out of the gate against an overmatched Titans defense. Prescott had already helped stake the Cowboys to a 27-6 lead by halftime with eight- and 10-yard touchdown strikes to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, respectively. Prescott would strike again through the air in the second half with an 11-yard touchdown pass to Javonte Williams before closing out his scoring strikes with a two-yard toss to Brevyn Spann-Ford with just under five minutes remaining. Prescott added his second rushing touchdown of the campaign on a two-yard run in the latter portion of the third quarter, giving him his second straight five-TD performance. Prescott is up to 3,049 passing yards and a 25:6 TD:INT heading into a Thanksgiving Day home clash with the Eagles in Week 12.

short_comment: Winters (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's clash against the Titans, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.
long_comment: Winters has hurt in the second quarter and had to be helped off the field by trainers. He was initially deemed questionable to return before being ruled out in the second half. Winters will finish the game with two tackles (both solo). The Cowboys next play on Thanksgiving against Philadelphia, and it's unclear if Winters will be able to suit up for that contest.

short_comment: Barham (hip/groin) is inactive for Sunday's game versus Tennessee.
long_comment: Barham didn't practice on Friday due to hip and groin issues. He was listed as questionable for Sunday's meeting with the Titans, though he has since been ruled out. With the rookie unavailable to play in Week 11, DeMarvion Overshown could see more snaps.

short_comment: Schoonmaker (illness) is active for Sunday's Week 11 matchup against Tennessee.
long_comment: Schoonmaker was unable to practice Thursday or Friday because he was under the weather, but the tight end appears to be feeling well enough to suit up Sunday. Meanwhile, Jake Ferguson (knee/ankle) will miss his second straight game, opening the door for Schoonmaker to potentially log a larger workload than usual on offense. With Ferguson out last Sunday versus San Francisco, Schoonmaker posted a season-high 35 percent offensive snap share and caught one of two targets for 12 yards.

short_comment: Corbin was elevated from the Cowboys' practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Corbin signed with the Cowboys' practice squad Nov. 4, and Saturday was his first elevation to the 53-man roster. With Tyler Goodson (knee) and Malik Davis (hip) both on injured reserve, Corbin will operate as Dallas' RB2 behind workhorse Javonte Williams. Corbin last saw regular-season action in 2023, when he appeared in six games as a member of the Giants.

short_comment: Thompson (hamstring) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Titans, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
long_comment: Thompson was a full participant in practice both Thursday and Friday, but the veteran safety is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve. He'll end up missing an eighth consecutive game due to a hamstring injury he picked up in Week 3 against the Ravens. Thompson's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.

short_comment: The Cowboys placed Bland (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Bland was expected to miss multiple games due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the 49ers. His placement on IR means he's required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Jaguars on Sunday, Dec. 27. Ameer Speed and Cobie Durant are both in line for larger roles in Dallas' secondary in Bland's absence.

short_comment: Ezeiruaku (ankle) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
long_comment: Ezeiruaku didn't play against the 49ers in Week 10 due to an ankle injury. He's avoided an injury tag for Week 11 after logging a full practice Friday, and his return means less rotational snaps at the edge rusher position will be available for James Houston and Von Miller. Ezeiruaku has 32 tackles (16 solo), including 2.5 sacks, and one forced fumble across nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Turpin is expected to resume return duties on both kickoffs and punts Sunday against the Titans, Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News reports.
long_comment: The wide receiver had to sit for three games with a rib injury before coming back for last Sunday's loss to the 49ers, in which he fielded punts but not kickoffs. Turpin has 574 kickoff-return yards and 108 punt-return yards on the year.

short_comment: Spann-Ford caught one of three targets for 26 yards during the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
long_comment: Spann-Ford operated as the Cowboys' No. 1 tight end in Week 10 due to the absence of Jake Ferguson (knee). However, George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy were the top targets for Dak Prescott. Ferguson is expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks while recovering from his injury, so Spann-Ford should once again top the depth chart in Week 11 against a Titans team that has given up 40-plus points in each of its last two games.

short_comment: Aubrey made both of his field-goal attempts and went 2-for-3 on extra-point tries during the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
long_comment: Aubrey connected on 52-yard field goals in both the first and third quarters, although his PAT in the second missed wide left. It was the second missed extra-point try of the season for Aubrey and his seventh miss overall, although five of those failed kicks have come on field-goal attempts from 50-plus yards. The Cowboys will stay home for Week 11 against the Titans, who give up 26.6 points per game (27th in the NFL) and have yielded 40-plus points in each of their last two contests.

short_comment: Abanikanda reverted to the Cowboys' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
long_comment: Abanikanda made his 2026 regular-season debut against the 49ers in Week 10, when he operated as the Cowboys' RB2 behind Javonte Williams. Abanikanda finished that contest with two carries for eight yards and a two-yard catch on his lone target in what ended as a 46-40 loss for Dallas. With both Tyler Goodson (knee) and Malik Davis (hip) on injured reserve, Abanikanda figures to be elevated to the Cowboys' active roster for Week 11 against the Titans on Sunday.

short_comment: Flournoy tallied six catches for 71 yards and one touchdown on seven targets during Sunday's loss to San Francisco. He also recovered a fumble.
long_comment: Dallas played catch-up for much of the second half in the offensive slugfest, so quarterback Dak Prescott took to the air 51 times. Flournoy got seven of those targets, finishing third on the team behind George Pickens (18) and CeeDee Lamb (13). Flournoy's six receptions and 71 yards were both his second-highest figures so far this season, and the TD was his third in the past five weeks. That last stat in particular gives him relevance in most fantasy leagues, especially in matchups during which Prescott is expected to air it out often. The Cowboys will seek a much-needed win next Sunday at home against Tennessee.

short_comment: Ogbonnia (finger) has re-entered Sunday's matchup against San Francisco, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.
long_comment: Ogbonnia suffered a finger injury in the second quarter and was subsequently deemed questionable to return. However, he was able to get back on the field after halftime. Ogbonnia will thus continue to play a key role along Dallas' defensive line.

short_comment: Bryant returned to Sunday's game against the Raiders after making a brief visit to the sideline tent, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
long_comment: Bryant's time away from the field occurred in the middle of the third quarter. He'll look to build upon the 3-32-0 line on three targets that he accrued to that point in the contest.

short_comment: Humphrey (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Las Vegas.
long_comment: Humphrey will be a healthy scratch for a second consecutive game. His next chance to play is Week 12 against the Steelers on Black Friday, although Humphrey is unlikely to see the field unless a wide receiver ahead of him on the depth chart is not available.

short_comment: Jones (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
long_comment: Jones will miss a second consecutive game due to a hamstring injury, which limited his practice participation during Week 11 prep. JL Skinner and Taylor Rapp are the top candidates to start alongside Talanoa Hufanga at safety in the absence of Jones, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the Steelers on Black Friday.

short_comment: Ehlinger (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Broncos' emergency third quarterback against the Raiders on Sunday.
long_comment: As the emergency QB3, Ehlinger is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

short_comment: The Broncos elevated Schrader from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Susanna Weir of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Schrader's elevation is his third of the season, so he'll need to be signed to Denver's active roster in order to see game action for the team beyond Sunday. In his previous two appearances, the third-year pro played a total of two offensive snaps and nine snaps on special teams without recording any carries or targets. Schrader isn't likely to be much of a factor on offense Sunday against Las Vegas, as Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins should continue to lead the Broncos' backfield. However, Schrader could contribute as a kick returner -- he's tallied 68 yards on three kickoff returns this season.

short_comment: The Broncos signed Rapp from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
long_comment: Rapp was cut from the Broncos' active roster in early November before opting to stick around as a member of the team's practice squad. His elevation gives Denver more depth in the secondary in the event that Brandon Jones (hamstring) cannot play against the Raiders on Sunday.

short_comment: Hufanga (ankle) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
long_comment: Hufanga logged three consecutive full practices during Week 11 prep. The strong safety did not let his persistent ankle injury inhibit him during the week, clearing him of any injury designation that may have followed him into Sunday's contest.

short_comment: Lohner (foot) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
long_comment: The Broncos opened Lohner's 21-day practice window Wednesday. The tight end is not quite ready to make his season debut, as he is still tending to his recovery from a foot injury he sustained in the offseason. Lohner was a full participant in all three Week 11 prep sessions, meaning his odds of returning in Week 12 are quite good if he can continue to log full sessions.

short_comment: Moss (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
long_comment: Moss was a full participant in Friday's practice. The newly extended Broncos starter has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest. The team's Week 10 bye helped Moss rest and recover from the injury he sustained during the Broncos' Week 9 win over the Panthers.

short_comment: Waddle (concussion) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders after practicing fully this week.
long_comment: Waddle was limited to just 14 snaps and one catch for 22 yards before exiting the Broncos' Week 9 win over the Panthers with a concussion. Following a well-time Week 10 bye, Waddle has progressed through the NFL's concussion protocol, ensuring that Denver's top pass catcher -- who has recorded a 30/337/2 receiving line on 52 targets through nine contests -- will be available this weekend.

short_comment: Abrams-Draine (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
long_comment: The cornerback was a limited participant Wednesday. Abrams-Draine had to miss the Broncos' win over the Panthers in Week 9 ahead of the team's Week 10 bye. Now that he's had a week off to get healthy, he appears ready to play Sunday against Las Vegas.

short_comment: Prentice (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
long_comment: It appears Prentice entered the league's concussion protocol following the Broncos' Week 9 win over the Panthers. He had additional time to recover courtesy of the Week 10 bye, so the veteran fullback should be available for Sunday's AFC West tilt against the Raiders.

short_comment: Singleton recorded six tackles (two solo) during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers in Week 9.
long_comment: Singleton's six stops were a season low, but he still finished second on the Broncos in that category behind Jahdae Barron (eight). It's been a career year for Singleton, who is up to an NFL-leading 107 total tackles through nine regular-season games, which includes 2.0 sacks.

short_comment: Trautman caught two of three passes for 15 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
long_comment: Trautman failed to record a catch across six games between Weeks 2 and 7, but he has logged two receptions in each of his two outings. His 41 offensive snaps ended up being ahead of fellow tight end Evan Engram (38), although the latter has been more involved in the Broncos' offensive game plan than Trautman. The Broncos' next game takes place in Week 11 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 22.

short_comment: Mims caught one of two targets for zero yards, added a five-yard carry and returned three punts for 22 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
long_comment: Nineteen of Mims' 24 snaps came on offense, although he logged only two touches in the process. He hasn't seen more than four targets in a game this season, with most of his output coming on special teams as a returner on both kickoffs and punts. The Broncos are on a bye for Week 10, so their next game will take place in Week 11 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 22

short_comment: Franklin brought in three of four targets for 31 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
long_comment: Franklin drew a 27-yard pass interference penalty on the Broncos' second offensive play of the game, but the third-year wide receiver didn't log his first catch until early in the fourth quarter. He has operated in a rotational role for most of the season, and even with Jaylen Waddle in the league's concussion protocol, Franklin will likely maintain that workload following the Broncos' Week 10 bye.

short_comment: Engram caught four of five targets for 33 yards in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
long_comment: The four catches matched Engram's season high, and his 33 yards were his most since Week 5. It goes without saying, but Engram is well off the fantasy radar at tight end. He has 17 catches for 169 yards and one touchdown through nine games, averaging a career-low 18.8 yards per contest.

short_comment: Lutz went 2-for-2 on both his field-goal attempts and extra-point tries during Denver's win over Carolina on Sunday.
long_comment: Lutz's field-goal tries were good from 26 and 48 yards. The 32-year-old has now converted 16 of his 19 field-goal attempts and all 16 of his extra-point tries across nine appearances this season.

short_comment: Dobbins rushed four times for 18 yards and caught his only target for four yards during Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina.
long_comment: Dobbins saw 13 fewer carries than rookie running back Jonah Coleman (17-57-1) in the game. The four rushes were a season low for Dobbins, and he figures to continue to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield moving forward.

short_comment: Sutton caught five of nine targets for 45 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
long_comment: The five grabs and nine targets led the Broncos on the day, but Pat Bryant just edged him out for the receiving yards lead. The highlight of Sutton's solid performance was a three-yard TD from Bo Nix in the first quarter, as none of his receptions went for longer than 12 yards. Denver gets a well-timed bye in Week 10, but if Jaylen Waddle (concussion) isn't cleared to play on the other side of it, Sutton could see bigger volume in Week 11 against the Raiders. On the season, the long-time Bronco sports a 25-266-2 line on 46 targets through nine games.

short_comment: Coleman carried the ball 17 times for 57 yards and a touchdown and caught all four of his targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
long_comment: The rookie has seized control of the lead-back role for the Broncos, with his 21 touches dwarfing J.K. Dobbins' five, and Coleman's nine-yard TD run early in the fourth quarter put his team in the lead for good. Coleman has piled up 261 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns over the last three games, and there's no reason to think his role will shrink on the other side of a Week 10 bye.

short_comment: Williams brought in all four targets for 93 yards and a touchdown in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
long_comment: The highlight of Williams' afternoon was a 57-yard touchdown reception early in the third quarter where he got free on a post pattern, and the fifth-year veteran also led the Lions in receiving yards. Williams has at least four receptions in four of the last five games, and Sunday marked his third game with more than 90 receiving yards. The 2022 first-round pick is now averaging 17.0 yards per reception heading into Thursday's Week 12 home matchup against the Bears.

short_comment: Goff completed 20 of 28 passes for 279 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while adding five rushes for 12 yards in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
long_comment: Goff put together an efficient effort on an afternoon where he recorded completions to eight different targets. The veteran signal-caller hit Amon-Ra St. Brown (14 yards) and Jameson Williams (57 yards) for his pair of touchdown passes, and he has multiple scoring strikes in two straight. Goff has a sparkling 20:4 TD:INT heading into a Thanksgiving Day showdown against the Bears at Ford Field on Thursday.

short_comment: St. Brown brought in five of six targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
long_comment: St. Brown set the pace for the Lions in catches while also tying for the team lead in targets, and the sure-handed receiver also recorded his eighth touchdown reception of the season on a 14-yard grab early in the second quarter that opened the scoring for either team. St. Brown's yardage total left plenty to be desired, but he's still up to a 70-792-8 line on 97 targets heading into Thursday's holiday showdown at home against the Bears.

short_comment: Gibbs rushed 23 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns and secured four of five targets for 20 yards in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
long_comment: Gibbs unsurprisingly had his work cut out for him against the Buccaneers' typically stingy run defense, but the Lions had the luxury of continuing to pound Gibbs into the line while protecting a second-half lead. Gibbs eventually broke through for a game-long 26-yard run and cashed in with one- and four-yard touchdown runs in the fourth quarter to help ice the victory. While Gibbs fell just short of his fifth 100-yard effort in the last six games, the 2023 first-round pick is up to 13 rushing touchdowns and is averaging 5.0 yards per carry heading into a Thanksgiving Day home showdown against the Bears.

short_comment: Dorsey (wrist) has re-entered Sunday's matchup against Tampa Bay, Justin Rogers of DetroitFootball.net reports.
long_comment: Dorsey hurt his wrist early in Sunday's game and was initially deemed questionable to return. The veteran cornerback has since been able to re-enter the game, albeit with a club over the hand that he injured. Dorsey has been working in a rotational role at cornerback, logging a defensive snap share between 32 and 38 percent three straight weeks.

short_comment: Rakestraw (shoulder) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
long_comment: A shoulder injury limited Rakestraw's practice reps during Week 11 prep. He was initially tagged as questionable, but after he went through pregame warmups, medical staff has determined that Rakestraw is not in good enough shape to suit up for Sunday's contest. With D.J. Reed (hip) also sidelined, Khalil Dorsey figures to start opposite Rock Ya-Sin at outside cornerback. Rakestraw's next opportunity to play is Thanksgiving Day against the Bears.

short_comment: Lacy (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
long_comment: Lacy was limited in practice all week due to a shoulder injury, but he's been cleared to play in Sunday's home game. He's expected to take on an elevated role at defensive end in the absence of Aidan Hutchinson, who is out for the rest of the season due to a torn ACL. Lacy has accumulated 12 tackles (four solo) through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Reed (hip) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
long_comment: Reed expressed pessimism Wednesday that he would be cleared to return for Week 11 due to a hip injury, and the veteran defensive back will, in fact, be sidelined for a third consecutive game. Khalil Dorsey will likely start opposite Rock Ya-Sin at outside cornerback in the absence of Reed, whose next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bears on Thanksgiving Day.

short_comment: Vaki (ankle) is listed as active Sunday versus the Buccaneers.
long_comment: Vaki has been tending to an ankle issue for three weeks running, but he's still suited up on the previous two occasions, combining for nine carries for 42 yards (4.7 YPC) and three catches (on three targets) for 19 yards. With active status confirmed for Week 11, he'll continue to serve as a complement to No. 1 RB Jahmyr Gibbs.

short_comment: The Lions placed Mays (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Mays missed the Lions' two prior games due to an ankle injury that he sustained against the Vikings in Week 8. His placement on IR means he's required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against Minnesota. Juice Scruggs figures to be the Lions' starting center for as long as Mays is sidelined.

short_comment: McCreary recorded six tackles (four solo) and two pass defenses (including an interception) during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots in Week 10 in Munich.
long_comment: McCreary recorded his first interception of the season in Week 10, when he jumped in front of a pass from Tommy DeVito -- who took over under center for the Patriots after Drake Maye injured his ankle in the first quarter -- that was intended for Mack Hollins, although the Lions' offense couldn't convert the takeaway into points. McCreary is up to 38 tackles (28 solo), including 1.0 sacks, 10 pass defenses and one forced fumble across nine regular-season games.

short_comment: The Lions activated Joseph (knee) from the reserve/PUP list Wednesday.
long_comment: Joseph was a full participant in his return to the active roster Wednesday. The free safety is set to make his 2026 debut in Week 11 against the Buccaneers, finally reuniting with strong safety Brian Branch after both spent lengthy periods on the Lions' reserve lists.

short_comment: The Lions placed Hutchinson (knee) on injured reserve Wednesday.
long_comment: Hutchinson's move to IR was merely a formality after he was diagnosed with a torn ACL in his right knee following his early exit from this past Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. The No. 2 overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft has now succumbed to two season-ending injuries through his first five years in the league, after a fractured tibia and fibula in his left leg cut short his 2024 campaign.

short_comment: Conklin went without a target while playing 22 of the Lions' 71 offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich.
long_comment: A healthy inactive for two of the Lions' first four games of the season, Conklin has now suited up for five consecutive contests. However, the veteran tight end has been handling a limited role, logging less than one-third of the offensive snaps in any of his seven appearances on the season while compiling a 2-11-0 receiving line on three targets.

short_comment: Saylors rushed twice for nine yards while adding 26 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots.
long_comment: Saylors played six snaps on offense while serving as a No. 3 option behind Jahmyr Gibbs and Sione Vaki in the backfield. Saylors was on the field for 20 snaps with the special-teams unit, and he'll continue to be primarily a special-teams asset in Week 11 against the Buccaneers.

short_comment: Wright caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich.
long_comment: Wright tied season highs in both receiving yards and catches during Sunday's win, and his 39 snaps on offense were second-most among Lions tight ends behind Sam LaPorta (56). Wright has accumulated seven catches on eight target for 42 yards across nine regular-season games, and he's mostly served as a blocking tight end on the Lions' offense.

short_comment: LaPorta caught one of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munch.
long_comment: The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early, and LaPorta simply didn't get many chances to make an impact. It was the worst performance of the season for the fourth-year tight end, but LaPorta's gone four straight games without reaching 40 receiving yards or getting into the end zone. He'll try to break out in Week 11 against the Buccaneers.

short_comment: Bates made all five of his PATs in the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich.
long_comment: Bates did not attempt a field goal in the contest. He remains 16-for-17 on field-goal attempts and moves to 29-for-29 on PATs through nine regular-season games in 2026.

short_comment: TeSlaa caught two of five targets for 19 yards and a touchdown during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich. He also recorded a tackle.
long_comment: It was a quiet day for TeSlaa, with the Lions' offense being powered by usual suspects Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs, with the latter duo combining for four touchdowns (three receiving, one rushing). TeSlaa was the other Lions player to find the end zone, which took place early in the second quarter on a 12-yard touchdown pass from Jared Goff. It was the first touchdown catch of the season for TeSlaa, who found the end zone six times across 17 regular-season games during his rookie campaign in 2025. He has been the Lions' distant WR3 behind St. Brown and Jameson Williams, and that shouldn't change ahead of the team's Week 11 tilt against the Buccaneers on Nov. 22.

short_comment: Johnson handled the first RB reps during the open portion of Sunday's practice, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
long_comment: Josh Jacobs logged his first official practice Sunday since undergoing finger surgery on Nov. 13, going down as a limited participant. Head coach Matt LaFleur relayed to Wes Hodkiewicz of the team's official site earlier in the day that Jacobs is "gonna have to show a lot of progress" the next few days to be available in Week 12. If Jacobs isn't active Wednesday at the Rams, Johnson may be the favorite to lead Green Bay's backfield in carries and rushing yards, as he did in a Week 10 loss to the Vikings, when he took 10 rushes for 42 yards. Meanwhile, fellow RB MarShawn Lloyd had seven touches for 39 yards from scrimmage in that contest, and Chris Brooks logged three touches for three total yards.

short_comment: Parsons (knee) practiced in a limited capacity Sunday, Rob Demovsky of ESPN reports.
long_comment: For a third week in a row, Parsons has maintained limited listings on Packers injury reports as he strives for his first game action since Dec. 14, 2025, when he tore the ACL in his left knee. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported earlier Sunday that Parsons is "on track" to return to action Wednesday versus the Rams, but first Green Bay will need to activate him from the reserve/PUP list for him to have a chance to do so.

short_comment: Jacobs (finger) was listed as limited at Sunday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN reports.
long_comment: With the Packers playing Wednesday against the Rams, the team posted an official practice report Sunday, and Jacobs was one of nine players deemed limited in the session. While it's encouraging that the running back was able to get some work in Sunday, Wes Hodkiewicz of the team's official site noted earlier Sunday that coach Matt LaFleur indicated Jacobs will "have to show a lot of progress" over the next couple days to be available versus Los Angeles. If Jacobs remains out Wednesday, Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks would be in line to handle Green Bay's backfield duties in his absence.

short_comment: Rhyan (ankle) was a limited practice participant Sunday, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Rhyan suffered an ankle injury against Detroit in Week 7 and hasn't played since. In fact, he hadn't practiced in any capacity until his limited session Sunday. Rhyan's ability to get in some reps suggests that he's progressing in his recovery, though it remains to be seen if he'll be able to return to action Wednesday versus the Rams.

short_comment: Franklin (shin) was listed as a limited practice participant for Sunday's session, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: A shin injury has prevented Franklin from playing in each of the Packers' last four games. A full practice over the next two days would probably be enough for him to return for Week 12 against the Rams on Wednesday.

short_comment: Cisse (ribs) was a limited participant in Sunday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Cisse is working through a rib injury that he picked up during the Packers' Week 10 loss to the Vikings. If he can log a full session over the next two days, then he would be on track to play against the Rams on Wednesday.

short_comment: Moore (ankle) was a limited participant in Sunday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Moore tweaked his ankle during the Packers' 30-10 loss to the Vikings in Week 10. He's mostly operated as a returner on kickoffs and punts this season, so those return duties would fall to Savion Williams, Matthew Golden and Bo Melton (thigh) if Moore is unable to play against the Rams on Wednesday.

short_comment: Melton (thigh) was a limited participant in Sunday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Melton's practice reps Sunday were limited due to a thigh injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Vikings. His practice participation over the coming days will shed light on his chances of playing Wednesday against the Rams.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Saturday that he doesn't anticipate Musgrove (neck) returning from the PUP list this season, according to NFL reporter Jason B. Hirschhorn.
long_comment: LaFleur acknowledged that Musgrove is still in the process of rehabbing the neck injury he sustained during OTAs in June, and the Packers haven't yet prepared for the tight end to resume practicing. Barring dramatic progress in his recovery over the next month, Musgrave looks like he'll be sidelined for the final season of his rookie deal before hitting free agency in the spring.

short_comment: Williams logged eight tackles (two solo) and a pass defense during the Packers' 30-10 loss to the Vikings in Week 10.
long_comment: Williams played every single defensive snap in Week 10 and finished tied for the second-most tackles on the Packers behind Isaiah McDuffie (10). Williams has recorded at least eight stops in three of his last four outings and is up to 84 tackles (50 solo), including 1.0 sacks, eight pass defenses (including three interceptions) and a fumble recovery through 10 regular-season games. He is well on track to surpass 100 tackles for a second consecutive year.

short_comment: McKinney registered six tackles (three solo) and an interception during the Packers' 30-10 loss to the Vikings in Week 10.
long_comment: McKinney picked off a deep pass from Kirk Cousins intended for Tai Felton late in the second quarter, although the Packers' offense failed to turn that takeaway into points before the end of the half. McKinney has three picks over his last two outings and is up to a league-leading six interceptions. The veteran safety is up to 44 tackles (25 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and seven pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.

short_comment: out
long_comment: out

short_comment: Williams caught two passes for 27 yards on two targets in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: As he's been doing since making his season debut in Week 6, Williams operated as the Packers' third receiver against Minnesota. He logged 20 offensive snaps and ran 16 routes on 37 dropbacks. Williams has yet to hit 50 receiving yards in any of his five games this season and has no real fantasy appeal in 12-team fantasy leagues. He's well behind Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft in the order for touches and targets.

short_comment: Brooks rushed two times for one yard and caught his only target for two yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: It was Brooks' first action since Week 4 after spending five games on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. With Josh Jacobs (finger) inactive against Minnesota, Brooks led the backfield with 26 offensive snaps in Week 10, but it didn't translate to touches or opportunities to handle the football. With Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd also involved, it's difficult to pinpoint any of these three as reliable fantasy options despite Jacobs' absence.

short_comment: Sturdivant caught two passes for 37 yards and a touchdown on four targets in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: After Green Bay was shut out in the first half, Sturdivant's first career touchdown came in the third quarter from 32 yards out, and it went down as the Packers' lone touchdown of the afternoon. Sturdivant played just nine offensive snaps as the fourth receiver and would need more than one injury ahead of him on the depth chart to be relevant in fantasy.

short_comment: Smack went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made his only extra-point try during Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: Smack pushed a 53-yard field-goal try wide right in the first quarter before later converting a 40-yard attempt in the final seconds of the third quarter. The rookie has now gone 15-for-21 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-4 from 50-plus yards, while making 21 of 24 extra-point attempts over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

short_comment: Taylor completed one of two pass attempts for three yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: Down 20 points with four minutes remaining in the fourth quarter and with starting quarterback Jordan Love having already taken eight sacks on the afternoon, the Packers opted to turn to Taylor to direct the offense for their final possession of the day. All three of Taylor's appearances on the season have now come late in blowout wins or losses, and his opportunities are likely to remain limited to garbage-time situations so long as Love is healthy.

short_comment: Lloyd finished Sunday's loss to Minnesota with 13 yards on four carries while catching all three of his targets for 26 yards.
long_comment: With Josh Jacobs (finger) sidelined, Green Bay turned to the trio of Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks in the backfield. Johnson led the team with 10 carries and 42 total yards despite not getting any targets. Meanwhile, Lloyd turned his seven touches into 39 yards, and Brooks tallied just three yards on his three touches. Green Bay is on bye during the coming week, but Jacobs may still miss the team's next game, which will take place Wednesday, Nov. 25, against the Rams. If that's the case, Lloyd will likely work as part of a shared backfield again, which isn't great for his fantasy outlook.

short_comment: Kraft caught one of four targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: The tight end's numbers reflected how much time his quarterback had to look downfield, as Jordan Love got sacked eight times in the rout. Kraft has been held to just one catch in back-to-back games, and he heads into a Week 11 bye with a 37-370-3 line on 56 targets through 10 games, with the Rams as the next opponent on the horizon in Week 12.

short_comment: Golden caught five of nine targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: The second-year wideout was the only Packer to have much success on offense, leading the team in catches, targets and receiving yards. Golden has reached 70 yards in three straight games and five of the last six, and he heads into a Week 11 bye with a 58-853-5 line on 101 targets through 10 contests. His next chance to add to those numbers will come in Week 12 against the Rams.

short_comment: Watson caught three of five targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to Minnesota.
long_comment: The Packers' passing game was stifled as the Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times, giving him little time to find receivers like Watson. The 37 yards were a season low for the fifth-year wideout, while the three grabs tied for his lowest volume of 2026. Watson will take a 52-916-7 line on 79 targets through 10 contests into a Week 11 bye before facing the Rams in Week 12.

short_comment: Love completed 17 of 27 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: The 28-year-old QB came into the game having been sacked just 17 times in his first nine games of the season, but Minnesota brought Love down eight times Sunday. Despite that onslaught, he was able to find J. Michael Sturdivant for a 32-yard TD in the third quarter to salvage his line slightly. It was the first time since Week 6 that Love had failed to throw multiple touchdowns, and just the second time all season. He'll get a Week 11 bye to heal up from Sunday's pummeling before facing Myles Garrett and the Rams in Week 12.

short_comment: Glover (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
long_comment: Glover's practice reps were limited during Week 10 prep due to a knee injury that prevented him from playing against the Patriots in Week 9. The third-year pro was cleared by medical staff to play Sunday, and he should reclaim his starting role at right guard from Laken Tomlinson.

short_comment: Stewart played 17 special-teams snaps in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday night.
long_comment: With the return of Reed Blankenship to the starting lineup, Stewart was relegated to special teams. The strong safety played 17 snaps but did not appear in the box score.

short_comment: To'oTo'o accumulated six tackles (four solo) in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday night.
long_comment: To'oTo'o played 100 percent of the Texans' defensive snaps for the second straight week. The linebacker was on the field for all 48 plays, logging four solo tackles in the effort.

short_comment: Anderson logged five tackles (two solo), including 1.0 sacks, during the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday night.
long_comment: Anderson extended his NFL sacks lead to 11.5 in Thursday's contest. The pass rusher is amassing another strong season to contend for Defensive Player of the Year. Anderson finished 2025 with 12.0 sacks and is set to surpass that personal record this season.

short_comment: Moreau brought in his lone target for eight yards during the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
long_comment: Moreau's 30 offensive snaps were second among Texans tight ends behind Dalton Schultz's 34, yet it was Marlin Klein who led the position group with four catches (on as many targets) for 24 yards, including a 13-yard touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud late in the third quarter. Moreau is up to a 12-80-3 receiving line on 15 targets through 10 regular-season games and has caught one pass or zero in five of those contests. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal unless Schultz were to miss time.

short_comment: Fairbairn made his sole field-goal attempt and all three PATs in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday night.
long_comment: Fairbairn's only field goal of the night was a 27-yarder with 15 seconds remaining in the first half. The kicker is 20-for-21 on field-goal attempts and 27-for-27 on PATs over 10 regular-season games so far in 2026.

short_comment: Demercado rushed five times for 33 yards and caught both of his targets for minus-four yards in Thursday night's 26-3 win over the Colts.
long_comment: With Woody Marks (concussion) inactive, Demercado played the complementary role behind lead back David Montgomery, who rushed 26 times for 107 yards in his return from a multi-week groin injury. Demercado was picked up off waivers from Dallas last month.

short_comment: Boutte's hip injury he suffered in Thursday night's win over the Colts doesn't appear to be serious, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
long_comment: The wideout had one of his more productive games of the season before being injured, as he caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown. His 40 yards were the second-most he's produced in a game this season. Boutte is up to 21 grabs for 359 yards and three touchdowns on 31 targets across 10 games in 2026.

short_comment: Hutchinson caught two of three targets for 13 yards in Thursday night's 26-3 win over the Colts.
long_comment: Hutchinson played 54 of 66 offensive snaps, second at wide receiver on the team behind Nico Collins' 59, and the former has been operating as the Texans' WR2 in terms of playing time for the last several weeks. By not scoring a touchdown Thursday night, Hutchinson snapped his personal three-game touchdown streak. For the season, he has 30 catches for 358 yards and three scores on 57 targets. He's on pace to set new career highs across the board.

short_comment: Klein secured all four targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
long_comment: Klein surprisingly outpaced veteran position mates Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau on the night, and the rookie second-round pick, whose only other career reception coming in was a 16-yard grab in Week 1, added his first career touchdown on a 13-yard catch in the third quarter. Given Klein had been a complete non-factor coming into the night, it's difficult to predict whether Thursday's production will have any carryover to a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Schultz brought in his only target for 11 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
long_comment: Schultz had a minimal role on a night when C.J. Stroud threw for a modest 194 yards and recorded completions to nine different targets. The veteran tight end now has consecutive one-catch, 11-yard tallies after recording multiple receptions in each of his first eight games of the season, and Schultz's production will remain hard to trust heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Dell secured three of four targets for 27 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
long_comment: The speedy wideout finished tied for second in receptions for the Texans on a night when C.J. Stroud recorded completions to nine different targets overall. Dell has played an effective complementary role since making his return from a gruesome 2024 knee injury in Week 7, as he now has an 11-196-1 line and four catches of 20-plus yards across 18 targets heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Stroud completed 21 of 26 passes for 194 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed six times for 27 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
long_comment: Stroud's night got off to a rocky start when a deflected pass resulted in an interception on the Texans' opening drive, but the red-hot signal-caller was near perfect from that point forward. The 2023 first-round pick went on to toss three touchdown passes for the second straight game and multiple scores for the fifth consecutive contest overall. Stroud connected with Nico Collins (42 yards), Kayshon Boutte (24 yards) and Marlin Klein (13 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes, and he'll take a sparkling 22:4 TD:INT into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Collins secured three of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
long_comment: Facing a Colts defense down both Sauce Gardner (calf) and Charvarius Ward (knee), Collins looked primed for a big night early when he recorded a 42-yard touchdown grab to cap off Houston's second possession. However, C.J. Stroud proceeded to spread the ball around to nine different targets overall, leading to Collins tying his second-lowest reception tally and posting his third-lowest yardage total of the season. However, the star wideout did extend his touchdown streak to three games, and he'll next take aim at what has been an inconsistent Ravens secondary in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Montgomery rushed 26 times for 107 yards and brought in three of four targets for 17 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
long_comment: Making his return from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, Montgomery functioned as the clear lead back with Woody Marks (concussion) unavailable. The former put together the best rushing yardage total of his brief Texans tenure, handling his highest number of carries since Week 4 of his 2023 debut campaign with the Lions. Montgomery also was encouragingly involved in a complementary role in the passing game, and he'll now have some extra time to recover from Thursday's workload ahead of a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29. However, if Marks is able to clear concussion protocol ahead of that contest, Montgomery will see his touch count take a hit.

short_comment: Rutledge (stinger) was deemed questionable to return near the end of Thursday's 26-3 win against Indianapolis and didn't end up re-entering the game.
long_comment: The Texans announced Rutledge's injury in the waning moments of the contest, but he had been in the medical tent well before that time. Febechi Nwaiwu took over at left guard following Rutledge's departure. With Houston not set to play again until Sunday, Nov. 29, against Baltimore, Rutledge will look to recover from the stinger in time to suit up.

short_comment: Brown (back) has returned to Thursday's game versus the Colts, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
long_comment: Brown left Thursday's contest after suffering a back injury, but he was able to check back in with the Texans' field goal team in the second quarter. With that said, veteran Braden Smith was still working as Houston's right tackle when the first half of Thursday's game ended.

short_comment: Rankins (ankle) is questionable to return to Thursday's game versus the Colts.
long_comment: Rankins sustained an apparent ankle injury during the second quarter of Thursday's contest, and he was able to walk gingerly to the sideline under his own power. In his absence, rookie second-rounder Kayden McDonald figures to see an increase in snaps on the defensive line.

short_comment: Braswell has been ruled out for the remainder of Thursday's game versus the Colts with a knee injury.
long_comment: Braswell suffered an injury in kick coverage on the opening kickoff and was promptly carted off the field with his right leg in an air cast, per James Boyd of The Athletic. The Texans will have to try to find a way to replace his production on special teams.

short_comment: Teller (back) is inactive for Thursday's game versus the Colts.
long_comment: Teller was unavailable in Week 10 against the Browns due to an illness, and he'll be sidelined in Week 11 by a back injury. In his absence, rookie fourth-rounder Febechi Nwaiwu projects as the Texans' top option off the bench at guard.

short_comment: Hummel (groin) is active for Thursday Night Football against the Colts.
long_comment: The linebacker suffered the injury in Week 1, returned for Week 10 and then carried a questionable tag into this contest, but he appears ready to play through the injury for the second consecutive game. Hummel logged two tackles (one solo) across 21 special-teams snaps against the Browns last week.

short_comment: Smith (hamstring) is active for Thursday night's game against the Colts.
long_comment: The cornerback was activated from injured reserve earlier in the day Thursday and will be making his first appearance since Week 4. Smith played just seven defensive snaps across the first four games of the season.
