short_comment: Pierce's season "is almost certainly over" due to the heel injury that landed the wideout on IR on Sept. 26, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network.
long_comment: The 3-8 Colts traded both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen ahead of the NFL trade deadline, and now it appears they'll err on the side of caution with Pierce for the remainder of what has turned into a lost season for the team. With that in mind, Pierce will be able to turn his focus toward returning to full health in advance of the 2027 NFL campaign. Heading into next Sunday's game against the Giants, the Colts will proceed with a WR corps comprised of Laquon Treadwell, Deion Burks, Anthony Gould, Ashton Dulin, Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and Quez Watkins.

short_comment: Boettcher recorded six tackles (three solo) during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.
long_comment: Boettcher finished Thursday's game tied for the fourth-most tackles on the Colts. The rookie fourth-rounder has started in each of Indianapolis' last three games, which has lined up with the absence of Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee, IR). Boettcher is up to 50 tackles (16 solo) through 11 regular-season games.

short_comment: Adebawore finished Thursday's 26-3 loss to the Texans with seven tackles (four solo), including 1.0 sacks.
long_comment: Adebawore recorded his fifth sack of the season early in the third quarter, when he took down C.J. Stroud for a seven-yard loss. Adebawore has already set a career-high in sacks through 11 regular-season games and has accumulated 31 tackles (15 solo), one defense and a scoop-and-score in 2026.

short_comment: Haulcy logged nine tackles (four solo) and an interception during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.
long_comment: The rookie third-rounder recorded the first interception of his career in the first quarter, when a pass from C.J. Stroud intended for Nico Collins bounced off Haulcy's helmet, off the hands of Cam Bynum and into Haulcy's arms. The LSU product is up to 53 tackles (30 solo) and three pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.

short_comment: Allen posted 16 tackles (seven solo) during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.
long_comment: It was a busy night for the rookie second-rounder, who finished with a career-high in stops while logging double-digit tackles for the third time this season. Allen has 45 total tackles over his last four outings, and most of that extra playing time has come in the absence of Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee, IR).

short_comment: Watkins caught one of his three targets for 26 yards during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night.
long_comment: Watkins played just five offensive snaps for the Colts in Thursday night's game. Despite playing only 10 percent of the offensive snaps, Watkins totaled the third-highest yardage by Colts pass catchers on the night with his 26-yard grab. The reserve wide receiver could see an expanded role down the stretch as the Colts experiment with starting quarterback Anthony Richardson in what is all but a lost season.

short_comment: Dulin caught two of his four targets for 30 yards and assisted on two tackles on kick coverage during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night.
long_comment: Dulin played 22 offensive snaps and 10 special-teams snaps in the contest. The No. 4 wide receiver saw plenty of attention, catching 50 percent of his targets to accumulate the second-highest receiving yardage for the Colts, behind Anthony Gould's 48 yards.

short_comment: Burks was targeted three times for zero catches, had one kick return for 10 yards and made one tackle on kick coverage during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night.
long_comment: Burks was the No. 2 wide receiver for the Colts in the contest. Despite being targeted three times, the wide receiver could not haul in any passes from since-cut quarterback Daniel Jones. Burks played 32 offensive snaps and two special-teams snaps in the contest.

short_comment: Shrader went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.
long_comment: Shrader opened Thursday's scoring with a 34-yard field goal early in the first quarter. Those ended up being the only three points scored by the Colts, as Shrader missed a 56-yarder later in the quarter, and his 62-yarder in the second quarter was blocked by Logan Hall. It was the second time this season that Shrader has missed two kicks, and the third-year kicker now is 24-for-28 on field-goal attempts (including 9-for-12 on kicks from 50-plus yards) and 19-for-20 on extra-point tries through 11 regular-season games. His scoring potential figures to be lower for the rest of the season after the Colts waived Daniel Jones on Friday, which paves the way for Anthony Richardson to start under center in Week 12 against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: The Colts announced Friday that Leonard will act as Anthony Richardson's backup at quarterback, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: The Colts released starting quarterback Daniel Jones after a disastrous 26-3 Thursday night loss to the Texans in Week 11. With Richardson in line to start moving forward, Leonard is the next QB up on the depth chart. The second-year pro has been with the Colts since 2025, when he played in five games, completing 39 of 67 attempts for 415 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. He also rushed six times for 27 yards and two touchdowns.

short_comment: Head coach Shane Steichen announced Friday that Richardson will be the Colts' starting quarterback moving forward after the team waived Daniel Jones.
long_comment: Richardson made a cameo in Thursday's 26-3 loss at Houston, taking over for Jones for Indianapolis' final possession, but the former logged just a two-yard carry and two incompletions before the Texans ate up the final 6:50 of the contest. A 2023 first-round pick, Richardson himself hasn't started since Week 16 of the 2024 campaign, making just four brief appearances the past two seasons combined, but he'll have a chance to boost his value (or not) in the final year of his rookie contract.

short_comment: Giddens rushed one time for five yards and caught his lone target for 11 yards in Thursday night's 26-3 loss to the Texans.
long_comment: With Seth McGowan (hamstring) exiting early with an injury, Giddens spelled Jonathan Taylor and played seven offensive snaps. Through three games this season, Giddens has rushed seven times for 48 yards and registered one catch for 11 yards. If McGowan's injury costs him time, Giddens figures to handle RB2 duties in his absence.

short_comment: Treadwell failed to catch his lone target in Thursday night's 26-3 loss to the Texans.
long_comment: Treadwell played a position-high 40 of 50 offensive snaps but continues to run wind sprints in an offense that doesn't throw the ball down the field. Through 11 games this season, Treadwell has just 19 catches for 239 yards and one touchdown on 33 targets.

short_comment: Gould secured two of three targets for 48 yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.
long_comment: Gould was the rather unlikely leader in receiving yards for the Colts on the night, with a team-high 31-yard catch playing a big role in getting him there. The 2024 fifth-round pick has seen an expanded role in the wake of the trades of Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, and for as long as Alec Pierce (IR, heel) is sidelined, Gould could function as one of Indianapolis' top downfield threats for either Daniel Jones, Anthony Richardson or Riley Leonard.

short_comment: Warren brought in one of five targets for 22 yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.
long_comment: The talented tight end's production continued to suffer collateral damage from Daniel Jones' poor play, but Warren did provide a useful gain on his one catch. The 2025 first-round pick now has recorded Thursday's yardage total or less in three of the last four games, but Warren's outlook may change if Jones, who James Boyd of The Athletic reports head coach Shane Steichen wouldn't rule out demoting when asked after the game, is replaced by Anthony Richardson or Riley Leonard under center.

short_comment: Taylor rushed 11 times for 21 yards and brought in four of five targets for six yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.
long_comment: Taylor put some distance between himself and promising rookie backfield mate Seth McGowan in terms of workload, as the former outpaced his teammate in carries by an 11-3 margin, even with the latter exiting before halftime with a hamstring injury. However, the extra opportunity was a moot point, as Taylor couldn't find any space to operate as either a runner or receiver. Daniel Jones' mediocre play under center certainly isn't helping the ground attack's cause, and Taylor now has recorded less than 50 rushing yards in three of the last four contests. The star running back will have some additional time to prepare for a relatively favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: McGowan (hamstring) has been ruled out for the rest of Thursday's game against the Texans, Jane Slater of NFL Network reports.
long_comment: McGowan was injured just before halftime while returning a kickoff. He was deemed questionable to return at the beginning of the third quarter and subsequently was ruled out shortly thereafter. The rookie running back gained seven yards on three carries and caught his only target for one yard before exiting while adding 117 yards on three kickoff returns. Jonathan Taylor should continue to get most of the work at running back for the Colts for the rest of the game, and DJ Giddens should handle whatever backfield snaps that Taylor doesn't get.

short_comment: Rhodes (hamstring) is active for Thursday night's game against the Texans.
long_comment: Rhodes is the team's long snapper. He missed last Sunday's win over Miami.

short_comment: Gardner (calf) is inactive for Thursday night's game against the Texans.
long_comment: The cornerback has a history of calf issues, and the Colts, in the middle of a lost season, have no reason to push Gardner to play on a short week. With Charvarius Ward (knee) also out, Indy is down its top two cornerbacks against a pass-heavy Houston offense.

long_comment: Jones suffered a chest injury early in the first half, and his night has now officially come to a premature end. The Jaguars will now have to operate without their top slot cornerback for the stretch run versus New York.

short_comment: Dickerson (neck) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Giants.
long_comment: A neck injury limited Dickerson's practice reps during Week 11 prep, and he has not been cleared by medical staff to play in Sunday's contest. Ruke Orhorhoro and Davon Godchaux will both see a bump in rotational snaps on the defensive interior line in the absence of Dickerson, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the Titans on Nov. 29.

short_comment: Davis is slated to make his Jaguars debut Sunday against the Giants, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
long_comment: Acquired Nov. 9 in a deal with the Eagles, Davis didn't end up suiting up in the Jaguars' 40-23 win over the Titans last weekend while the Jacksonville coaching staff opted to give him more time to get acclimated to his new team. After a full week of practice, Davis should be ready to step into a starting role at defensive tackle.

short_comment: Bates is slated to make his Jaguars debut Sunday against the Giants, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
long_comment: Acquired Nov. 9 in a deal with the Falcons, Bates didn't end up suiting up in the Jaguars' 40-23 win over the Titans last weekend while the Jacksonville coaching staff opted to give him more time to get acclimated to his new team. After a full week of practice, Bates should be ready to step into a starting role at safety alongside Antonio Johnson.

short_comment: Green (forearm) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants.
long_comment: Green has strung together six consecutive full practices since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 11. He's not quite ready to be activated from IR, so his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 29. Green is in the final stages of his recovery from an elbow injury that he suffered in Week 1 against the Browns.

short_comment: Walker (ribs) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.
long_comment: Walker was a full participant in Friday's practice, and that was enough for the fifth-year defensive end to avoid an injury tag heading into Sunday's contest. The 2022 first-rounder has 22 tackles (10 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and two pass defenses through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Johnson (ankle) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Giants.
long_comment: Johnson was a limited participant in all three Week 11 practices, but the 2023 fifth-rounder has done enough to avoid an injury tag ahead of Sunday's contest. Johnson has accumulated 40 tackles (23 solo), including 1.5 sacks, and one pass defense across eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Allen (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.
long_comment: Allen has next to no fantasy appeal having played a total of 73 offensive snaps this season. In nine games, he's touched the ball a total of three times on offense.

short_comment: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.
long_comment: The backup running back has been dealing with the hand issue for weeks but continues to play through it. Rodriguez has averaged an underwhelming 3.9 yards per carry on 59 attempts this season, allowing Bhayshul Tuten to run away with lead-back duties in Jacksonville.

short_comment: Meyers (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.
long_comment: Meyers has been playing through the ankle injury for weeks, so his status was never in real doubt despite limited practices all week. The veteran wideout doesn't have a touchdown catch since Week 3 and has topped 65 receiving yards in a game just once all season. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling fantasy option.

short_comment: Tuten (ankle/foot) was present for the stretching portion of Friday's practice before moving to a side field, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
long_comment: Tuten was deemed limited at practice Wednesday and then was a non-participant Thursday. It remains to be seen how the Jaguars classify his participation (or lack thereof) in Friday's session, with added clarity on that front set to arrive via the team's upcoming injury report.

short_comment: Oluokun finished Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans with 10 tackles (nine solo).
long_comment: Sunday was the third time in nine regular-season games that Oluokun played every single defensive snap and the second time that he reached double-digit tackles. His nine solo stops were a season high and most in a game since Week 1 of the 2024 season. Oluokun has accumulated 44 tackles (30 solo), including 2.0 sacks, over his last five outings.

short_comment: Little went 4-for-4 on field-goal attempts and made all four of his PATs during Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
long_comment: Little was able to make four field-goal tries for the second straight week, converting attempts from 46, 48, 36 and 40 yards in the contest. The kicker has now gone 18-for-20 on field-goal attempts, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests during the 2026 campaign.

short_comment: Hunter caught both of his targets for 16 yards, recorded a three-yard carry and contributed five tackles (three solo) and an interception during the Jaguars' 40-23 win over the Titans on Sunday.
long_comment: Fifty-six of Hunter's 62 snaps Sunday came on defense, and that's where he made his biggest impact with a diving interception on a Cam Ward pass intended for Elic Ayomanor, and the Jaguars offense converted that takeaway into a field goal 10 plays later. Hunter's impact on both sides of the ball has been undeniable: he has 28 catches (on 45 targets) for 298 yards and a touchdown, along with 36 tackles (24 solo) and seven pass defenses (including three interceptions) through nine regular-season games. The Jaguars will hit the road for Week 11 against the Giants on Nov. 22.

short_comment: Cameron caught all three of his targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23, Week 10 win over Tennessee. He also returned five kickoffs for 142 yards.
long_comment: Cameron gave the Jaguars a 14-point lead early in the fourth quarter when he hauled in a 25-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence. It was the rookie wideout's third touchdown of the campaign but his first since Week 3. Cameron's 67 receiving yards marked a career high, while his three receptions tied the most he's had as a pro. Cameron's propensity for finding the end zone (his three TDs have come on just 12 total catches) is appealing, but at this point he isn't getting enough volume to be a reliable week-to-week fantasy asset.

short_comment: Downs brought in four of five targets for 59 yards in the Chiefs' 34-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Playing in his second game as a member of the Chiefs, Downs posted four receptions for the second consecutive contest and upped his receiving yardage total by six over that of his team debut. Downs' quick chemistry with Patrick Mahomes is certainly noteworthy and makes an already impressive air attack all the more effective heading into Thursday night's Thanksgiving road showdown against the Bills.

short_comment: Rice secured all six targets for 53 yards in the Chiefs' 34-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Rice tied for the team lead in receptions and finished as the runner-up in targets to Travis Kelce. The veteran receiver averaged a modest 8.8 yards per catch, his third game in the last four with under 10.0 yards per reception. Rice has at least five catches in four consecutive contests heading into Thursday's Week 12 Thanksgiving showdown against the Bills in Buffalo.

short_comment: Kelce brought in six of seven targets for 74 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs' 34-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Kelce tied for the team lead in receptions with Rashee Rice while setting the pace in both receiving yards and targets, and he recorded his first multi-touchdown effort of the season in the process. The legendary tight end recorded his scoring grabs from eight and 22 yards out, and both his reception and yardage totals were his highest since Week 2. Kelce will take a 41-586-4 line into Thursday's Thanksgiving Day road showdown against the Bills.

short_comment: Mahomes completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions in the Chiefs' 34-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Mahomes was clicking early against the Cardinals' defense, capping off the opening possession of the game with an eight-yard touchdown toss to Travis Kelce. The prolific signal-caller would go on to add a 22-yard scoring toss to Kelce shortly before the end of the first half, and he capped off his scoring strikes with an 18-yarder to Xavier Worthy in which the speedy receiver sped up the right sideline. Mahomes now has consecutive 300-yard efforts and has accomplished the feat in three of the past four games, affording him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 12 showdown with Josh Allen and the Bills on Thanksgiving Night.

short_comment: Johnson rushed 23 times for 105 yards and a touchdown and brought in all four targets for 38 yards in the Chiefs' 34-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Making a second consecutive start in place of Kenneth Walker (groin), Johnson once again provided starter-quality production as both a runner and receiver. The rookie also added his second career TD on a three-yard run late in the first quarter, making it an all-around rewarding fantasy day. The Chiefs expect Walker to be ready to return for a Thanksgiving Night showdown against the Bills in four days, but even if that comes to pass, Johnson has likely earned himself a larger role for the stretch run with his performance the last two contests.

short_comment: VanSumeren (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
long_comment: VanSumeran injured his knee in the second half, and with no other fullback on the 53-man roster, the Chiefs could turn to tight end Jake Briningstool to provide additional blocking out of the backfield. VanSumeran's status over the coming days will be worth monitoring, given that the Chiefs are operating on a short week and play against the Bills on Thanksgiving Day.

short_comment: Gray (ribs) is questionable to return to Sunday's matchup against Arizona.
long_comment: Gray's injury status was announced late in the game after Kansas City had already built an insurmountable lead, so it would be a surprise if the tight end returns to the contest. The bigger picture is the Chiefs' Thanksgiving matchup against Buffalo -- if Gray is dealing with a more-than-minor issue, his availability for that game could be in peril. Gray finished Sunday's matchup with three catches for 21 yards on five targets.

short_comment: Norman-Lott (knee) is inactive against Arizona on Sunday.
long_comment: Norman-Lott was activated from the Chiefs' reserve/PUP list Wednesday, but he was limited in all three practices during Week 11 prep and drew the questionable tag for Sunday's game. He's in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025, but he's not quite ready to make his return. Norman-Lott's next opportunity to make his 2026 regular-season debut is Thanksgiving Day against the Bills.

short_comment: Woods (neck) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
long_comment: Woods opened Week 11 prep with back-to-back full practices before having his reps limited Friday, which prompted the Chiefs to tag him as questionable. The rookie first-rounder has not been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday, so he will miss his third consecutive game due to a neck injury. Bryson Eason and Marcus Harris will continue to operate in rotational roles on the interior defensive line behind Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga in the absence of Woods, whose next chance to play is Thanksgiving Day against the Bills.

short_comment: Nussmeier (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Chiefs' emergency third quarterback against the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: The rookie seventh-rounder has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026. As the emergency QB3, Nussmeier is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

short_comment: The Chiefs elevated Carter from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
long_comment: Carter has been brought up from the practice squad for a second consecutive week to give the Chiefs more depth in the backfield in the absence of Kenneth Walker (groin). Carter operated as the Chiefs' RB2 behind rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson in Week 10 against the Falcons, but the former's role could be limited to special-teams duties since Jaydn Ott (hamstring) has been cleared to return from a one-game absence.

short_comment: Bolton (shin) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
long_comment: Bolton popped up on the Chiefs' injury report with a shin issue Wednesday, but it doesn't look like it was anything serious. He's fifth in the league in total tackles (89) going into a Week 11 matchup versus a pass-happy Cardinals offense.

short_comment: The Chiefs placed Wiley (ankle) on injured reserve Wednesday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
long_comment: Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter of the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons with an ankle injury. The tight end will now be on IR as he nurses his fractured ankle until at least the latter part of the regular season. Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool are now the only tight ends on the Chiefs' active roster.

short_comment: Ott (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
long_comment: Ott was unable to play against the Falcons in Week 10 due to a hamstring injury. However, the undrafted rookie out of Oklahoma was cleared to practice in full Wednesday, so he should be available for Sunday's home game against the Cardinals. If Kenneth Walker (groin) cannot play in Week 11, then Ott would have the opportunity to serve as the Chiefs' RB2 behind rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson.

short_comment: Tranquill recorded nine total tackles (six solo) during Sunday's 35-13 victory over the Falcons.
long_comment: Tranquill finished tied for the team lead in tackles with fellow linebacker Nick Bolton in Week 10, notching at least nine takedowns for the third time in four weeks after not having reached that mark in any of the team's first five games of the year. On the season, Tranquill has now produced 75 total tackles (39 solo), two passes defensed and a fumble recovery over nine contests so far.

short_comment: Williams recorded five total tackles (two solo) and two passes defensed, including an interception, during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
long_comment: Williams was able to register at least five takedowns for the third time this season, and his biggest moment of the game came in the fourth quarter when he intercepted a deep pass from Falcons quarterback Michael Penix. The interception was his second of the year, and he has now compiled 41 total tackles (23 solo) and 11 passes defensed over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

short_comment: Briningstool caught one of two targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 35-13 win against the Jets on Sunday.
long_comment: Briningstool connected with Patrick Mahomes for a 20-yard reception midway through the first quarter but didn't record another reception. The 23-year-old tight end has exactly one catch in each of his past three games. That's not enough production to warrant fantasy consideration, but Briningstool is at least showing growth as a pass catcher, as he had just one catch on two targets over his first six contests of the campaign.

short_comment: Butker made all five PATs in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
long_comment: Butker did not attempt a field goal in the contest, as the Chiefs solely scored touchdowns. He now moves to 27-for-28 on PATs in 2026 as he continues to struggle to hold onto the starting kicker job.

short_comment: Armstrong caught his only target for a 43-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
long_comment: The wideout played just 17 of 64 offensive snaps against Atlanta and ran only seven pass routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks. Armstrong was tasked with blocking duties on 10 of his snaps. He still managed to catch his first career touchdown in the fourth quarter with the game already well out of hand. Armstrong is not on the fantasy radar.

short_comment: Allen caught two of four targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
long_comment: The rookie wideout scored his first career touchdown by beating the cornerback on a stutter-go for a 39-yard touchdown in the third quarter. With Josh Downs still getting comfortable and learning the offense following Tuesday's acquisition from the Colts, Allen maintained a significant role on offense, playing 22 of 64 offensive snaps. Once Downs progresses from the 10 snaps he played against Atlanta, it will be interesting to see if Allen can push Xavier Worthy (zero catches on three targets across 56 snaps on Sunday) for a larger piece of the outside receiver role in Kansas City's offense.

short_comment: Worthy failed to catch any of his three targets in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
long_comment: Worthy ran a team-high 37 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks, but on a day Mahomes targeted nine different players, Worthy was the only one to not record a catch. With Josh Downs now in the fold and working to get comfortable in the offense, Worthy's role will likely only continue to shrink. On just eight routes in his team debut Sunday, Downs posted a 4-53-1 receiving line on five targets. Worthy hasn't produced that many fantasy points in a game all season. He's waiver-wire fodder in 12-team redraft leagues.

short_comment: Keenan (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's contest against Denver.
long_comment: Keenan went down with a knee injury in the first half, and he will now officially be sidelined for the rest of Week 11. With Adam Butler (concussion) also done for the day, JJ Pegues will handle the bulk of the workload at defensive tackle versus the Broncos.

short_comment: Butler (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's contest against the Broncos.
long_comment: Butler took a blow to the head late in the first half, and his night has now officially come to a premature end due to a concussion. With Tim Keenan (knee) also done for the night, JJ Pegues is the last man standing at defensive tackle for Las Vegas.

short_comment: Young (stinger) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against Denver.
long_comment: Young suffered a stinger late in the first half, and his availability for the rest of the game is now in question. In his absence, Cody White is a candidate to see a slight uptick in opportunities on offense with Las Vegas.

short_comment: With Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) inactive for Sunday's game against the Broncos, Mayer is in line to see an expanded role in Week 11.
long_comment: Mayer has already carved out his share of looks in the team's passing game, but the absence of Bowers -- who leads the Raiders with 70 targets and 50 catches in eight games played -- creates a big void at tight end on Sunday. In that context, Mayer figures to see added volume versus Denver and represents a viable pivot option for those who roster Bowers, or are otherwise in need of help at the position with six teams on bye.

short_comment: Thornton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's Week 11 tilt against Denver.
long_comment: Thornton is dealing with a back injury, but he wasn't listed on Las Vegas' practice report during Week 11 prep. As such, it appears the second-year wideout is a healthy scratch Sunday. Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor, Jack Bech, Dareke Young and Cody White will make up the Raiders' WR corps.

short_comment: Fatukasi (toe) is active against the Broncos on Sunday.
long_comment: Fatukasi was tagged as questionable due to a toe injury, although he ended Week 11 prep with a full practice Friday, and he's now been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday. The veteran defensive lineman has 16 tackles (four solo), including 1.0 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through 10 regular-season games.

short_comment: Gay (hip) is active for Sunday's game at Denver.
long_comment: Gay sandwiched two limited practices this week around Thursday's DNP due to a right hip injury and entered the weekend listed as questionable for Sunday. Because the Raiders didn't elevate Kansei Matsuzawa from the practice squad Saturday, it was an indication that Gay was good to go for Week 11, which now has been confirmed. In 10 games this season, Gay has connected on 21 of 23 field-goal attempts and all 22 point-after tries.

short_comment: Bowers (ankle/quad) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
long_comment: Adam Schefter of ESPN previously reported on Sunday NFL Countdown that there was "not a lot of optimism" that Bowers (who was in and out of last Sunday's loss to the Seahawks before exiting for good after halftime due to an ankle injury) would be available versus Denver. Now that he's been made inactive, Bowers -- who was limited at practice Thursday and Friday -- will target a potential Nov. 29 return, while fellow TE Michael Mayer is poised to step into a key role in the Raiders passing offense Sunday in his notable absence.

short_comment: The Raiders elevated Runyon from the practice squad Saturday.
long_comment: Las Vegas is bringing up Runyon due to Brock Bowers (ankle) being listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos. Runyon appeared in 13 games with the Raiders last season but logged just 45 offensive snaps and caught only one pass for three yards. He's depth behind Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas.

short_comment: Booker (ankle) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: An ankle injury has sidelined Booker for each of the Raiders' last two games. However, his full session Wednesday indicates that he's recovered from his injury and on track to play in Sunday's AFC West tilt against the Broncos. Booker has accumulated 13 tackles (nine solo) across seven regular-season games.

short_comment: Paye (neck) was not listed on the Raiders' injury report Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Paye made an early exit in the second half of Sunday's loss to the Seahawks with a neck injury. The linebacker did not return to the contest, but the issue does not seem to have been serious. Paye is healthy and appears ready to log consistent full practices throughout Week 11 prep.

short_comment: Chinn tallied seven tackles (three solo) in a loss to Seattle on Sunday.
long_comment: Chinn continues to put up consistent tackling numbers, as he's now logged at least seven stops in six straight games. The veteran safety has played all but one of Las Vegas' defensive snaps this season. He's up to 72 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception), two forced fumbles and two recovered fumbles through 10 contests.

short_comment: Walker posted eight tackles (four solo) and recovered a fumble against Seattle in Sunday's Week 10 loss.
long_comment: Walker, Nakobe Dean and Maxx Crosby all had eight tackles Sunday to co-lead the team. Walker added a fumble recovery on the second play of the game that helped set up a Raiders touchdown. The veteran linebacker has remained productive in his first season with Las Vegas following four years in Green Bay. Walker has 80 tackles, including 2.0 sacks, and two recovered fumbles though 10 contests on the campaign.

short_comment: Dean registered eight tackles (five solo) and recovered a fumble Sunday in a Week 10 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: Dean tied for the team lead in stops with Maxx Crosby and Quay Walker. Nonetheless, the veteran linebacker saw his five-game streak of double-digit tackles come to an end. Dean did contribute his first recovered fumble of the season when he scooped up a ball that was turned over by Seattle QB Drew Lock in the fourth quarter. Dean is tied with Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton for the NFL lead with 107 tackles, though Denver has played one fewer game.

short_comment: Crosby finished Sunday's loss to Seattle with eight tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks.
long_comment: Crosby tied for the team lead with his season-high eight stops. Among those tackles, four went for a loss, including a fourth-quarter sack of Drew Lock. After registering just a half-sack over six games from Week 2 to Week 7, Crosby has since finished with exactly 1.0 sacks in each of his past three contests. He's at 5.0 sacks overall through 10 games as he seeks a fifth NFL campaign with double-digit sacks.

short_comment: Bech caught two of seven targets for 10 yards during the Raiders' 21-13 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
long_comment: Bech was the favorite target of rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza, who was making his first career start Sunday after the Raiders shipped Kirk Cousins to the Vikings at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Bech's seven targets were a season high, but he mustered only two catches for his efforts, and he failed to connect on each of the last four passes he saw from Mendoza in the fourth quarter. The volume appears to be there for Bech, and he could take on a larger role offensively in Week 11 against the Broncos on Nov. 22 if star tight end Brock Bowers (ankle) is unable to play.

short_comment: Nailor recorded one reception for minus-1 yard on four targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: Making his first NFL start, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza was under siege throughout the afternoon, as a ferocious Seahawks defense sacked him six times and limited him to just 143 passing yards on 29 attempts. As a result, Nailor and the Raiders' other pass catchers were held quiet, with running back Ashton Jeanty (four receptions for 46 yards) being the only Las Vegas player to top two catches and 25 receiving yards. Though Mendoza will get some more favorable matchups over the Raiders' final seven games, Nailor will be difficult to count on for production. Even while Kirk Cousins served as the starting quarterback for Las Vegas before being traded to the Vikings last week, Nailor was limited to just 14 receptions for 122 yards and one touchdown on 28 targets through eight appearances.

short_comment: Laube played all 22 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks and returned two kickoffs for 46 yards and one punt for zero yards.
long_comment: Since earning seven touches in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Patriots, Laube has been an afterthought on offense. He's played just eight total offense snaps in the Raiders' ensuing five games, and Sunday marked the first time all season that he was limited exclusively to special teams.

short_comment: Mitchell (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Jets.
long_comment: Mitchell was briefly sidelined with a back injury in the first half before returning to action. The running back is now dealing with an apparent knee issue, placing some doubt on his chances to return to the field Sunday. In his absence, Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal will handle the bulk of the workload in the backfield.

short_comment: Mesidor (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Jets.
long_comment: Mesidor suffered an ankle injury during the first half, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. In the rookie's absence, Caleb Murphy and Bud Dupree are both candidates to see an increase in opportunities at outside linebacker behind starters Tuli Tuipulotu and Khalil Mack.

short_comment: Njoku (shoulder) has returned to Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Jets, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Njoku briefly exited in the first quarter after hurting his shoulder on a 13-yard catch. He was initially deemed questionable to return but has since re-entered the contest. The veteran tight end is playing just his second game after returning from a stint on IR due to a fibula injury.

short_comment: Pipkins (knee) is active for Sunday's matchup against the Jets.
long_comment: Pipkins had been on IR since late September before being activated Saturday. The veteran offensive lineman is now set to give the Chargers' offensive line a boost. Pipkins may work in a rotational role, as Logan Taylor is "locked in" at left guard, per Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com.

short_comment: Waxter (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Jets.
long_comment: Waxter was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury. His availability gives the Chargers another contributor on special teams and depth in the secondary.

short_comment: Still is inactive for Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Jets due to an ankle injury.
long_comment: Still wasn't on the Chargers' practice report until Friday, when he was a limited participant due to an ankle injury. Though he was initially deemed questionable, the third-year cornerback isn't going to be able to suit up against New York. Still's next chance to play will be in Week 12 against New England on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Thompson (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets.
long_comment: Thompson's inactive status doesn't come as much of a surprise, given that he entered the weekend as doubtful due to a hamstring injury. He hasn't played since Week 2 against the Raiders, and his next chance to see the field is Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29.

short_comment: Lambert-Smith (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets.
long_comment: With Ladd McConkey (back) active, Lambert-Smith will be a healthy scratch for Sunday's contest. Lambert-Smith's next opportunity to suit up is Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29, although his path to playing time is limited unless there is an injury in front of him on the Chargers' wide receiver depth chart.

short_comment: Kolar (concussion) is active for Sunday's game versus the Jets.
long_comment: Kolar showed up on the Chargers' first Week 11 injury report Wednesday as a non-participant due to a concussion, and thereafter he managed just one limited session Friday before the team tagged him as questionable for Sunday. Despite his inability to practice fully this week and the prospect of gaining clearance from an independent neurologist shaped up as a difficult combination to overcome, he's available to the offense. Kolar will join Oronde Gadsden and David Njoku as L.A.'s active tight ends this weekend.

short_comment: McConkey (back) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Jets.
long_comment: Though he wasn't among the Chargers' Week 9 inactives, back spasms led to McConkey not recording any snaps during the team's 44-22 loss to the Texans on Nov. 8.  After not traveling to Baltimore with his teammates for this past Monday's 23-20 win, the wideout was able to practice in a limited fashion Wednesday through Friday before carrying a 'questionable' designation into the weekend. With no known setbacks since, the 2024 second-rounder will give it a go and is on track to reclaim his key role in Los Angeles' WR corps alongside Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris. In the six games he's taken the field in, McConkey has averaged 2.8 catches (on 4.2 targets) for 47.7 yards with one TD, a pace that the 6-foot, 185-pounder figures to pick up if he can avoid injuries in the coming weeks.

short_comment: The Chargers placed Shelley (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Shelley was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets due to an ankle injury. His placement on IR means he must miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the 49ers on Thursday, Dec. 17. Shelley has contributed both on defense and special teams and has eight solo tackles and a pass defense across six regular-season games.

short_comment: Dupree requested his release from the Chargers earlier this week, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Dupree also asked for a trade earlier in the season, but the Chargers have so far not granted his request. The veteran edge rusher has been limited to special teams over the Chargers' last two games and has yet to record a sack. If he's let go by the Chargers, then Dupree could garner interest from teams looking for a boost in the pass rush.

short_comment: Eboigbe (ankle) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets.
long_comment: Eboigbe was unable to play against the Ravens this past Monday due to an ankle injury. He ended Week 11 prep with a full practice Friday, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag ahead of Sunday's contest. His return means there will be less rotational snaps at defensive end for rookie fifth-rounder Nick Barrett.

short_comment: Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel told reporters Friday that his "expectation" is that Hampton is the lead back for the Chargers, Omar Navarro of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: "Generally, my expecation is [Hampton] is our leading ball carrier every week.  ... I knew based on his last two practice weeks, we were feeling like he was going to have a breakout performance at any given time," McDaniel said Friday. That breakout game took place Monday against the Ravens, when Hampton turned 22 carries into a season-high 105 yards and a touchdown in a 23-20 win for the Chargers. With the Chargers getting extra time to rest, Hampton's stock is trending up heading into Week 12 against the Jets, whose defense ranks 30th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (135.3) and 29th in rushing touchdowns allowed (13).

short_comment: Tomlinson recorded five tackles (three solo) including 2.0 sacks during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
long_comment: In a game where Ravens quarterback Jacoby Brissett dropped back 51 times, there were no shortage of opportunities for the Chargers to rush the passer, and Tomlinson came away with the best single-game sack total of his nine-plus year career so far. He has taken on a larger role on the defensive line than 2025 third-rounder Jamaree Caldwell in recent weeks, and only Teair Tart played as many snaps on the Chargers' defensive front as Tomlinson did (36) in Week 10.

short_comment: Phillips recorded nine tackles (four solo) and an interception during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
long_comment: Phillips was in the right place at the right time when a Jacoby Brissett pass bounced off the helmet of rookie wideout Ja'Kobi Lane in the second quarter, and the turnover set up a Chargers touchdown that put the team ahead 17-7. His tackle total was also his highest going back to Week 18 of the 2023 season with the Ravens. With that said, his role in the Chargers' defense is still not big enough to warrant IDP consideration in most formats.

short_comment: Dicker made all three of his field-goal tries and converted both of his extra-point attempts during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
long_comment: Dicker's longest field goal on the day was only from 38 yards out, but his accuracy played a big part in the Chargers picking up their first win of the season. He hasn't missed a kick since Week 3, but the team's general inability to move the ball consistently keeps him from projecting as a top-tier fantasy option in most formats going into a Week 11 matchup versus the Jets.

short_comment: Gadsden hauled in his lone target for seven yards in Monday's 23-20 win over Baltimore.
long_comment: Gadsden went to the locker room during the first half of Monday's game after being poked in the ye, but the second-year tight end was cleared to return for the second quarter. However, his 12 offensive snaps were his lowest since Week 1 against the Cardinals (10), and that lack of playing time coincided with the return of veteran tight end David Njoku, who missed the Chargers' six prior games while on IR due to a fibula injury. Njoku and Charlie Kolar appear to be the Chargers' top options at tight end, squeezing Gadsden out of the game plan ahead of Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

short_comment: Vidal turned two carries into zero yards, brought in both of his targets for 14 yards and returned one kickoff for 32 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
long_comment: Vidal's 15 offensive snaps were just ahead of Keaton Mitchell's 13, but both running backs took a back seat to Omarion Hampton, who was on the field for 36 of the Chargers' 57 snaps on offense and led the backfield with 22 carries for 105 yards and one touchdown. Vidal's two carries were his fewest since Week 3 against the Bills (one), although his 15-yard catch early in the third quarter set the Chargers up just outside the red zone, with Cameron Dicker connecting on a 34-yard field goal four plays later. Vidal and Mitchell appear to be falling into rotational roles behind Hampton heading into Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

short_comment: Johnston brought in his sole target for six yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
long_comment: The speedster was poised to see some added involvement with Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, but that never materialized on a night when 86 of Justin Herbert's 129 passing yards went to Tre' Harris. Johnston's yardage total was a season-low figure, and he's now been limited to one reception in four of the last five games. Johnston's often been able to offset the modest catch totals with big plays, but that clearly wasn't the case Monday night. Johnston will remain a hit-or-miss fantasy option in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday, irrespective of McConkey's availability.

short_comment: Harris secured all five targets for 86 yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
long_comment: With Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, Harris functioned as a de facto top target for Justin Herbert, and he was responsible for all but 43 of his quarterback's passing yards. The yardage tally also was a career-high figure for Harris, who generated team-high totals with all three components of his receiving line. Harris is up to a career-high 348 receiving yards on 26 catches heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

short_comment: Williams (toe) was a limited practice participant Sunday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
long_comment: Head coach Sean McVay relayed to Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com on Saturday that Williams is dealing with a sore toe, so his practice restrictions to begin Week 12 prep aren't a surprise. Williams will have two more chances to put himself in a position to avoid a designation for Wednesday's game against the Packers.

short_comment: Adams (hamstring) has an "outside chance" to return from injured reserve for the Rams' Week 13 matchup with the Chiefs but is more likely to be activated around mid-December, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
long_comment: The Rams have seemingly discounted the possibility of Adams coming off IR for a Wednesday matchup with the Packers in Week 12, while a Week 13 return is more plausible but still sounds like a "long shot," according to Rapoport. Instead, the Rams' Week 14 game against the 49ers on Dec. 13 would appear to be the most realistic target for Adams' return, especially since Los Angeles will effectively have a "mini-bye" ahead of that contest following its Thursday night matchup with Kansas City on Dec. 3. Whenever he's reinstated from IR, Adams should be in store for heavy target shares in the Rams' remaining games after star wideout Puka Nacua (knee) underwent season-ending MCL surgery earlier this week.

short_comment: Nacua (knee/toe) is expected to be sidelined 4-to-5 months after undergoing surgery Tuesday to repair his right MCL, which means he won't be on track to return at any point during the playoffs, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
long_comment: Nacua is also dealing with a PCL sprain and turf toe, but the only procedure he required was for his MCL. With a firmer 4-to-5-month timeline now in place for the star wideout, he'll be done for the season while the Rams look to others to help fill the massive void in their receiver corps. Davante Adams (hamstring) should eventually take on a heavy target share, but he's also on injured reserve and isn't expected to return until at least Week 13. That leaves Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith as the current healthy wideouts on the team's 53-man roster ahead of next Wednesday's tilt versus the Packers. Nacua, who is in the final year of his rookie deal, is slated to become a free agent in March.

short_comment: Coach Sean McVay said Saturday that Avila (hamstring) will not play in Wednesday's game against the Packers, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
long_comment: The Rams' left guard was injured in Week 9 against the Commanders and will miss a second straight game. Bill Murray or Justin Dedich (undisclosed) projects to start in Avila's place versus Green Bay.

short_comment: The Rams opened the 21-day practice window for Dedich (undisclosed) on Saturday.
long_comment: Dedich opened the regular season on injured reserve due to an undisclosed injury. He's now been cleared to practice, and his participation over the next few days will factor into whether he's activated from IR ahead of Wednesday's game against Green Bay.

short_comment: The Rams designated Turner (groin) to return from injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Turner has missed the Rams' last four games while on injured reserve due to a groin injury that he sustained in Week 6 against the Cardinals. His practice participation over the coming days will ultimately determine whether he'll be activated from IR ahead of Wednesday's game against the Packers.

short_comment: The Rams are expected to lean more on Mumpfield and the rest of the team's wide receivers in the absence of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), the latter of whom is expected to be sidelined for the remainder of the regular season, Nate Atkins and Jonathan Jones of The Athletic report.
long_comment: Nacua is expected to miss "a couple of months" after undergoing surgery Tuesday to repair his MCL, per Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com. With Nacua and Davante Adams (hamstring, IR) sidelined for Week 10 against the Cardinals, Mumpfield operated as the Rams' WR1 for that contest and finished with three catches (on four targets) for 81 yards in a 34-6 win for Los Angeles. The Rams are "hopeful" that Adams will return soon, but if he's not activated from injured reserve ahead of Wednesday's game against the Packers, then Mumpfield would lead Los Angeles' wide receiver group that also includes Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith.

short_comment: Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) isn't ready to return to game action, but the Rams still plan to activate him from injured reserve before Week 12 and keep him on the active roster, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
long_comment: Even if Ferguson is moved back to the active roster, coach Sean McVay's comments indicate the tight end still won't be ready to play coming out of the team's Week 11 bye. His activation at least would keep him off season-ending IR, but his near-term availability remains uncertain until the Rams signal he's ready for game action. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) likely done for the remainder of the regular season following MCL surgery, Ferguson and Davante Adams (hamstring) are needed badly in this offense.

short_comment: Lake posted two tackles (one solo) during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals in Week 10.
long_comment: Lake recorded at least six tackles in each of the first nine games of the regular season, but he had only two stops in Week 10 despite playing every defensive snap. The fifth-year defensive back is up to 65 tackles (38 solo), 11 pass defenses (including three interceptions) and two forced fumbles through 10 regular-season games heading into the Week 11 bye.

short_comment: Klare went without a target while playing four of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: Klare has been a healthy inactive on three occasions this season, but he's now suited up in three straight games while the Rams have been short on pass-catching options due to injuries to tight end Terrance Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) and wideouts Puka Nacua (knee), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back). Despite those personnel losses, Klare has still struggled to carve out meaningful playing time, as fellow tight ends Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen are all regarded as superior blockers and have been prioritized ahead of him. The rookie second-round pick out of Ohio State still has yet to draw a target through his first seven NFL games.

short_comment: Daniels caught one of two targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) inactive, Daniels' 46 snaps were two fewer than Konata Mumpfield for the team lead at receiver for the Rams. Mumpfield led the group in targets (four), catches (three) and yards (81), and only Xavier Smith (2-40-1) joined him as wide receivers to catch more than one pass from Matthew Stafford against Arizona while the Rams relied heavily on their tight ends and running backs. Daniels' playing time isn't worth chasing in fantasy.

short_comment: Atwell caught one of two targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: Despite both Puka Nacua (toe/knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) being sidelined, Atwell still played just 16 of 76 offensive snaps versus Arizona and ran 15 routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks. Atwell played behind both Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels at receiver for Los Angeles.

short_comment: Rivers rushed 15 times for 81 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: Amazingly, all 15 of Rivers' carries came on the Rams' final drive of the game, where they ran 17 plays to kill the final 12 minutes and 15 seconds of the clock. Rivers rushed 15 straight times before Matthew Stafford performed a pair of kneel-downs to end the game. It will be interesting to see if Rivers' efficiency was enough to earn him more carries before garbage time moving forward, especially after Kyren Williams looked stuck in the mud against Arizona, rushing 12 times for just 23 yards. For now, Rivers is simply a name to keep an eye on over the next couple of weeks, with the Rams wanting to lean on the run due to all of their high-profile pass-catching injuries.

short_comment: Allen caught his lone target for a 19-yard touchdown in Sunday's win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: With all three of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) out, the Rams leaned on their tight-end triumvirate of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Allen, as all three played more offensive snaps than any of the Los Angeles wideouts. Parkinson (53 snaps) led the way, followed by Allen (52) and Higbee (51), and both Allen and Higbee caught touchdowns. Allen, however, ran just six routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks, so it's not enough to warrant consideration in fantasy leagues.

short_comment: McManus made both of his field-goal attempts and all four PATs in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: McManus' Sunday performance extends his perfect streak with a Rams' special teams unit that desperately needed consistency at kicker. He's now 5-for-5 on field-goal attempts and 14-for-14 on PATs after five regular-season contests as a Ram in 2026.

short_comment: Higbee caught three of four targets for 17 yards and a touchdown during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Higbee's third and final catch of Sunday's game came late in the second quarter, with the veteran tight end connecting with Matthew Stafford for a five-yard touchdown to give the Rams a 10-6 lead. It was the second touchdown of the season for Higbee, with his first taking place in Week 3 against the Broncos. He's been held to three catches or fewer in each of his last four games, although he's been on the field for at least 50 offensive snaps in three of those contests. The Rams are on bye for Week 11, and Higbee's limited target share will take a hit if Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

short_comment: Parkinson caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Parkinson was able to shed an injury designation for Sunday's game after having his practice reps limited during Week 10 prep due to a lingering rib injury. His second catch of the contest went for 10 yards early in the third quarter and set the Rams up on the 1-yard line, with Blake Corum finding the end zone on the next play. Parkinson was on the field for 53 of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps (69.7 percent), and fellow tight ends Davis Allen (52) and Tyler Higbee (51) were not far behind. The Rams are committed to using their 13-man personnel, although the game plan could be slightly tweaked after the Week 11 bye if wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Parkinson has caught 20 passes (on 25 targets) for 127 yards and a touchdown through eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Shelton (hamstring) is set to miss several weeks due to injury, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
long_comment: The starting center is set to miss 4-6 weeks with a hamstring injury. Shelton will likely be placed on injured reserve while he recovers. Dylan McMahon (knee, IR) also sustained an injury in the Rams' Week 10 win over the Cardinals, leaving Beaux Limmer to finish out the contest at center and to likely fill in as the starter for the foreseeable future.

short_comment: The Rams placed McMahon (knee) on injured reserve Monday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
long_comment: McMahon suffered a knee injury during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. The injury is severe enough for McMahon to require a stint on IR, so he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, with his next chance to play being Week 16 against the Seahawks on Christmas Day. With Coleman Shelton nursing a hamstring injury, the Rams may have to turn to other options like David Quessenberry or Beaux Limmer to fill in at center for the time being.

short_comment: McCord completed 12 of 33 passes for 102 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills. He also rushed twice for nine yards.
long_comment: McCord has thrown for just 311 yards without a touchdown pass in his first two NFL starts. The 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles is poised to make at least two more starts while Malik Willis (abdomen) is on IR. Miami's lone win of the season came against the Jets, whom the Dolphins will host in Week 12.

short_comment: Gordon rushed 11 times for 69 yards while catching two of three targets for minus-2 yards in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills.
long_comment: After a quiet first half, Gordon got free for a 24-yard run on the first possession of the second half to set up Miami's third and final field goal of the afternoon. Gordon was Miami's most effective offensive player as usual, as Kyle McCord threw for just 102 yards in the latter's second NFL start. This was Gordon's seventh consecutive game with at least 64 scrimmage yards, but he'll take a four-game touchdown drought into a Week 12 home game against the Jets.

short_comment: Brents (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's tilt against Buffalo.
long_comment: Brents was hurt in the fourth quarter and is uncertain to re-enter the contest. Darrell Baker has taken over for Brents at outside cornerback.

short_comment: Bell (chest) has returned to Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: Bell suffered a chest injury late in the first half and was subsequently deemed questionable to return. However, the rookie wideout got back into the game shortly after halftime. Bell will look to be more productive after finishing the first half without a reception.

short_comment: Savaiinaea (ankle) has been cleared to return to Sunday's game against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: Savaiinaea injured his ankle in the second quarter, but the second-year pro is back on the field for the start of the second half. He'll return to his normal spot at right guard while Jarrett Kingston shifts to the sidelines.

short_comment: Simpson (knee) is listed as inactive for Sunday's matchup against the Bills.
long_comment: Simpson was previously doubtful for Sunday's game after not practicing Wednesday or Thursday and ending the week with limited participation. The 26-year-old plays the majority of snaps on special teams, so his absence shouldn't greatly impact the defense.

short_comment: Brewer (concussion) is active for Sunday's matchup versus Buffalo.
long_comment: Brewer missed last Sunday's game against Indianapolis due to a concussion, but he's since cleared the NFL's five-step protocol, including being cleared by an independent neurologist. As such, the All-Pro will be able to return to his usual role as the anchor of Miami's offensive line at center.

short_comment: Baker (knee) is active for Sunday's battle against the Bills.
long_comment: Baker had been on the reserve/PUP list all season before being activated Saturday. He logged a week of full practices, which led to the veteran cornerback being active for what will be his Dolphins debut Sunday. Baker may initially work in a rotational role behind starters JuJu Brents and Jason Marshall.

short_comment: Trader (shoulder/groin) is inactive for Sunday's Week 11 tilt against Buffalo.
long_comment: Trader's inactive status is not surprising given that he didn't practice all week and entered the weekend tagged as doubtful to suit up. Sunday will mark the second-year pro's first career absence. Kyle Louis and/or Zayne Anderson could get a big bump in work at safety in Trader's stead.

short_comment: The Dolphins elevated Carlson from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
long_comment: Carlson signed with the Dolphins' practice squad Tuesday, two weeks after being released by the Saints. Following the Dolphins' release of Zane Gonzalez, Carlson will operate as Miami's kicker for Sunday's game against Buffalo. In seven appearances with the Saints this season, Carlson went 8-for-12 on field-goal attempts (including 3-for-7 on kicks from 50-plus yards) and 16-for-18 on extra-point tries.

short_comment: Meyer (neck) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: Meyer suffered a stinger against the Colts in Week 10, but his full practice Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's AFC East game. He would likely start at center for a second consecutive week if Aaron Brewer (concussion) is not cleared to play.

short_comment: Douglas (shoulder) will play Sunday against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: Douglas was managed during the practice week, but he's good to go for his normal every-down role Sunday against Buffalo. With the Dolphins installed as 16.5-point underdogs, Miami is projected to throw a ton in comeback mode. However, Douglas is a tough click for fantasy with Kyle McCord under center.

short_comment: Phillips underwent surgery on his injured bicep Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: Phillips was recently placed on injured reserve with a season-ending biceps injury sustained in Week 10 versus the Colts. The 22-year-old ends his season with 28 tackles (11 solo) through nine games. Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper are top candidates to see more reps at defensive tackle as the season continues.

short_comment: Brooks produced nine total tackles (six solo), a pass defensed and a forced fumble during Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
long_comment: Brooks was able to register at least nine takedowns for the fourth straight game and seventh time overall this season. The linebacker was also able to strip Colts running back Jonathan Taylor in the first quarter, but offensive lineman Dalton Tucker was able to jump on the loose ball. Brooks is now up to 84 total tackles (38 solo) while also adding two passes defensed and a forced fumble over nine contests to open the 2026 season.

short_comment: Rodriguez recorded one solo tackle during Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
long_comment: Rodriguez finished with fewer than eight takedowns for just the third time this season, and his one tackle was a season low for the rookie. The linebacker has now compiled 80 total tackles (36 solo), including a 1.0 sacks, while also adding an interception and a forced fumble over nine contests so far during his rookie campaign.

short_comment: Taaffe recorded six total tackles (four solo) and an interception during Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
long_comment: Taaffe was able to register at least six stops for the third straight game and sixth time overall this season. The safety's biggest moment of the game came in the second quarter, when he jumped in front of a short pass from Colts quarterback Daniel Jones, securing his third interception of the year. On the year, Taaffe has compiled 53 total tackles (27 solo), three interceptions and a forced fumble over nine contests so far.

short_comment: Johnson recorded four total tackles (three solo) and a pick-six in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
long_comment: Johnson was able to secure an interception for the second straight week, jumping in front of a pass from Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in the third quarter, ultimately returning the interception for a 59-yard touchdown. The cornerback has now registered 46 total tackles (24 solo), four passes defensed and a forced fumble over nine games this season.

short_comment: Coleman logged one catch for six yards on six targets in Sunday's Week 10 loss to Indianapolis.
long_comment: Coleman couldn't get on the same page as QB Kyle McCord, who made his first NFL regular-season appearance. In fact, Coleman has been quiet inefficient regardless of who has thrown him the ball this year, as he has just nine receptions on 27 targets through nine games. Two of his nine catches have been touchdowns, but he's not getting enough touches to be a trustworthy fantasy option.
