short_comment: Bartholomew should revert to a backup role with T.J. Hockenson returning from a wrist injury for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
long_comment: Bartholomew was targeted four times in Week 10 for three catches, 36 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers. The tight end received more than one target in only one other game this season, Week 5, when Hockenson went down after two offensive snaps. While Bartholomew has proven himself a red-zone threat, Hockenson should return to seeing most of the tight end volume in Sunday's contest.

short_comment: Jones (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.
long_comment: Jones -- who was managing a shoulder injury during Week 11 prep -- was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He was signed to the Vikings' 53-man roster Wednesday to give the team more depth at wide receiver while Jordan Addison recovers from a thumb injury. Jones figures to be limited to a rotational role on offense while serving as a contributor on special teams.

short_comment: Van Ginkel (quadriceps) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.
long_comment: Van Ginkel's practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday while managing a quadriceps injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Packers. He was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for the veteran edge rusher to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. In Van Ginkel's four outings since the Vikings' Week 6 bye, he has accumulated 14 tackles (eight solo), including 4.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery.

short_comment: Cashman (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.
long_comment: Cashman will end up missing one game (Week 10 against the Packers) while in the league's concussion protocol, and his return means Ivan Pace will revert to a rotational role at inside linebacker for Sunday's contest. Cashman has accumulated 76 tackles (41 solo), including a career-high-tying 4.5 sacks, seven pass defenses and one fumble recovery across eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Hockenson (wrist) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday night's game against the 49ers.
long_comment: After sitting out last Sunday against Green Bay and then logging limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, Hockenson is ready to return against San Francisco in a potential playoff preview. His lack of a designation puts Minnesota's top tight end in position to reclaim his usual role in the passing game that now has Kirk Cousins at quarterback. Hockenson is a TE1 for fantasy purposes.

short_comment: Wilson recorded seven tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, during the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers in Week 10.
long_comment: The Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times in Week 10, with Wilson taking down the Packers quarterback for a six-yard loss early in the second quarter. Wilson has logged at least 0.5 sacks in three of his last four outings, and the veteran linebacker is up to 57 tackles (30 solo), including 4.0 sacks, and one pass defense through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: The Vikings placed Richter (foot) on injured reserve Wednesday.
long_comment: Richter will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a foot injury during the Week 10 win over the Packers. The 26-year-old has compiled six tackles (three solo) across nine appearances this season while playing almost exclusively on special teams.

short_comment: Jennings (calf) practiced in full Wednesday.
long_comment: Jennings sat out the last two games due to a calf injury, but his return to all activity Wednesday gives the Vikings' receiving corps a boost after Jordan Addison was lost for at least a few weeks due to a broken thumb that required surgery. As for Jennings, he'll have a prime opportunity to work opposite No. 1 WR Justin Jefferson as he looks to build upon his 6-54-0 line on 10 targets in his six appearances this season.

short_comment: Reichard made all three of his field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers on Sunday.
long_comment: All three of Reichard's field goals came from fewer than 40 yards out in the contest. The return of Kirk Cousins allowed Minnesota's offense to surge to its highest touchdown total since Week 1, the team's first bout against the Packers. Reichard is now 23-for-25 on field-goal attempts and remains perfect at 13-for-13 on PATs over nine regular-season games in 2026.

short_comment: Price is set for an increase in offensive workload with Jordan Addison (thumb) sidelined, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Price reeled in a season-high four passes for 49 yards and a score during Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. The wideout was operating in a more prominent offensive role for the second week in a row with Jauan Jennings (calf) sidelined, and fellow wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) was unable to play as well. Addison now is expected to undergo thumb surgery, opening the door for Price to operate in an elevated position in Minnesota's offense for the time being.

short_comment: Felton is on track to operate in a more prominent role in Week 11 versus the 49ers, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Felton drew a start in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, reeling in a season-high three of five targets for 33 yards over 56 offensive snaps. The wide receiver stepped into a starting role as a result of Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf) being sidelined, and Addison is now reportedly set to undergo surgery to address his injury, opening the door for more opportunities for Felton moving forward.

short_comment: Jones carried the ball 11 times for 47 yards and a touchdown and caught his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
long_comment: Jordan Mason led the Vikings with 59 rushing yards, but Jones had the more productive afternoon as he scored his first TD since Week 5 on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Jones' upside will remain limited while working in a timeshare with Mason, but he's still got some utility heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.

short_comment: Mason carried the ball 16 times for 59 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
long_comment: The fifth-year RB led the Vikings in rushing yards, but Aaron Jones was the more productive player in the backfield, gaining 55 scrimmage yards on 12 touches and scoring on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Mason has yet to get into the end zone in four games since returning from a thumb injury, piecing together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry while working in a timeshare with Jones. He could break that drought in Week 11 in a potential revenge game against the 49ers.

short_comment: Cousins completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. He added 11 rushing yards on three carries.
long_comment: Brought back to Minnesota at the trade deadline to stabilize the offense, Cousins did exactly that, connecting with Myles Price for a 38-yard TD in the first quarter and Gavin Bartholomew on a 20-yard score in the fourth while guiding Justin Jefferson to season highs in catches and targets. The Vikings' passing game didn't need to over-extend itself, however, as the defense sacked Jordan Love eight times in another dominant performance. Cousins may need to find another gear in Week 11 against the 49ers, but he'll have another week of practice to re-familiarize himself with Kevin O'Connell's scheme first.

short_comment: Jefferson caught nine of 13 targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
long_comment: In Kirk Cousins' return to the Vikings, Jefferson led the team in catches, targets and receiving yards, although Myles Price and Gavin Bartholomew were on the other end of the QB's two touchdown passes. The nine grabs and 13 targets were season highs for Jefferson, while the yardage total was his best showing since Week 5. Despite a disappointing 40-467-4 line on 64 targets through eight games, the star wideout's outlook for the rest of the year is pointed up heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.

short_comment: Metellus (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Packers.
long_comment: Metellus was added to the Vikings' practice report Friday due to a shoulder issue, but the injury won't prevent the seventh-year pro from suiting up for Sunday's NFC North showdown. He has 58 tackles (29 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and four pass defenses through eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Wentz (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Green Bay, but Kirk Cousins will be Minnesota's starting quarterback.
long_comment: Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out for another week but may eventually replace Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback. Wentz's miserable performance against the Bills last week likely was a factor in the Vikings trading for Cousins.

short_comment: Dallas caught his only target for a two-yard gain in Monday's Week 9 loss to the Bills.
long_comment: Dallas notched just eight offensive snaps but also contributed 19 snaps on special teams. The veteran running back went without a carry for the fourth time over Minnesota's past five games, indicating his lack of a role in the running game. Overall this season, Dallas has been a very small part of the Vikings' offense, recording four carries for 14 yards and five catches for 36 yards (on five targets) through eight contests.

short_comment: Maye, who sustained a fractured right fibula in last Sunday's loss to the Lions, is on track to miss at least six weeks, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
long_comment: The timetable put forth by Rapoport suggests that Maye could make a run at a late-season return, or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Given that the Patriots are already close to the limit of how many players they can designate for return from injured reserve, Maye isn't a lock to land on IR, but he's nonetheless facing an absence longer than the required four games that a placement on IR would mandate. For now, Tommy DeVito has been installed as the team's starter ahead of its Week 12 matchup against the Chargers, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup.

short_comment: Head coach Mike Vrabel said Friday that DeVito will start in Week 12 against the Chargers on Nov. 29, Mike Reiss and Adam Schefter of ESPN.com report.
long_comment: Drake Maye was diagnosed with a fractured right fibula, which he sustained in the first quarter of the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich. DeVito filled in for the rest of that contest and completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards, one touchdown and one interception while turning four carries into 19 yards. DeVito looks like he'll be New England's starter coming out of the bye, with rookie seventh-round pick Behren Morton operating as the backup.

short_comment: Brown (hamstring) is expected to miss multiple weeks, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
long_comment: New England's trade for Brown is going down as one the team would definitely prefer to reverse. He's shown no chemistry with Drake Maye (ankle) and hasn't looked healthy since injuring his ankle in the first half of the Week 1 game against the Seahawks. Brown also appears to have lost multiple steps with his downfield speed due to the laundry list of lower-body injuries that now includes ankle, knee and hamstring issues in 2026. The Patriots will play out the string on a lost season without Maye and Brown for several more weeks. Look for Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs (shoulder, IR) when healthy, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism to pick up the slack at wideout with Brown on the shelf again.

short_comment: Elliss logged 10 tackles (three solo) during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich.
long_comment: Week 10 was the third time this season that Elliss posted double-digit stops, and he ended up co-leading the Patriots in tackles with safety Kevin Byard. Through 10 regular-season games, Elliss has accumulated 75 tackles (37 solo), including 1.5 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so Elliss's next opportunity to suit up is Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Byard registered 10 tackles (three solo) and two pass defenses (including an interception) during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich.
long_comment: Byard picked off a Jared Goff pass intended for Jameson Williams in the end zone late in the second quarter, which halted the Lions' red zone drive in its tracks. It was the first time this season that Byard posted double-digit stops, and each of the veteran safety's two interceptions on the year have come over his last three outings. He enters the Week 11 bye with 53 tackles (26 solo) and five pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.

short_comment: Williams failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
long_comment: Williams did have a 21-yard carry late in the third quarter, although the play was nullified by offsetting penalties. It was the second straight game that the second-year wide receiver did not record a catch and the fifth time in 10 regular-season contests. New England is on a bye for Week 11, but the offense's outlook looks grim given that franchise quarterback Drake Maye is expected to miss time due to an ankle injury that he sustained in the first quarter of Sunday's game. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Larison turned his lone carry into two yards and caught two of three targets for 15 yards and a touchdown during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich. He also recorded a tackle on special teams.
long_comment: The Patriots lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury early in the first quarter, so backup Tommy DeVito was under center for most of contest. New England struggled with DeVito at the helm, but he did connect with Larison for a 10-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter in what was the Patriots' lone trip to the end zone. Even though that score came in garbage time, it was the first touchdown of Larison's NFL career, although he's firmly entrenched as the team's RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so their next game will take place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Chism did not catch his only target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss against the Lions in Munich in Week 10.
long_comment: A.J. Brown (hamstring) returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries in Week 10, and as a result, Chism saw his lowest snap count this season (8) since he was a healthy scratch in Week 1. His role coming out of the Patriots' bye in Week 11 will probably depend heavily on the availability of Brown, who picked up a hamstring issue against the Lions.

short_comment: Raridon caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich.
long_comment: The rookie tight end played his normal allotment of plays, seeing 62.7 percent of the offensive snaps, but the offense as a whole was broken after Drake Maye went out with an ankle injury early in the first quarter. The offense bogged down with Tommy DeVito at the controls, and Raridon's one target was his fewest in a game since Week 2. Raridon also has been held to single-digit receiving yards in two of the last three contests. He's averaging a robust 13.6 yards per catch this season but isn't a reliable fantasy option with Hunter Henry healthy.

short_comment: Borregales made his sole field-goal attempt and one PAT in the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich on Sunday.
long_comment: Borregales made a 33-yard field goal on the first drive of the game. The kicker is now 11-for-13 on field-goal attempts and 24-for-25 on PATs through 10 regular-season games in 2026.

short_comment: Douglas caught one of three passes for four yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
long_comment: The Patriots' offense was effective on the first drive of the game, but that was where the good news ended for New England after Drake Maye was knocked out for the rest of the contest due to an ankle injury. Tommy DeVito took over under center, and the offense struggled to move down the field for the rest of the game. For Douglas, it was the third time this season that he was held to one catch, with the last instance taking place in Week 3 against the Jaguars. A.J. Brown -- who was cleared to return from a two-game absence due to knee and ankle injuries -- also picked up a hamstring injury during Sunday's game, so Douglas could be the New England's WR1 following the Week 11 bye. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Henry caught two of three passes for 22 yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
long_comment: Both of Henry's catches of 10 and 12 yards came on the Patriots' first offensive drive of the game, which ended with a 33-yard field goal by Andy Borregales. Unfortunately for the Patriots, Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury on the play prior to the field goal and was unable to return, and the offense struggled to move down the field with backup Tommy DeVito under center. Maye will undergo more tests once the team has returned to home soil, but the good news for the Patriots is that they are on a bye for Week 11, so the third-year quarterback has more time to heal before New England's next game in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29. Henry's two catches Sunday were his fewest since Week 3 against the Jaguars (one), and the veteran tight end has a 34-383-2 receiving line on 40 targets through 10 regular-season games.

short_comment: Hollins caught five of six targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.
long_comment: In his second game back from a calf injury, Hollins led the Patriots in catches and receiving yards, but the entire offense was compromised when Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early. A.J. Brown (hamstring) also didn't last long in his latest return to action. New England gets a bye in Week 11, giving the team's injured stars a chance to recover, so Hollins' role and usage may not become clear until after the break. Over six appearances this season, Hollins has produced a 23-293-1 line on 32 targets.

short_comment: Kiner carried the ball 10 times for 25 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to Detroit.
long_comment: Rhamondre Stevenson was active despite dealing with a knee issue during the practice week, but the veteran back gained just four yards on six carries, and Kiner wound up leading the Patriots' backfield in both volume and yardage. The entire offense struggles after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, however. New England gets a Week 11 bye, so Kiner's role and usage for a Week 12 clash with the Chargers likely won't become clear until the health of Stevenson and Maye come into focus after the break.

short_comment: Stevenson carried the ball six times for four yards and caught his only target for one yard in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.
long_comment: The whole Patriots' offense struggled after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, but Stevenson also didn't look to be in peak form after dealing with a knee issue during the practice week. Corey Kiner wound up leading the backfield with just 25 rushing yards on 10 totes. Stevenson will get a Week 11 bye to rest up, and if Maye's injury ends up sidelining him for an extended period, New England could lean heavily on its running game in Week 12 against the Chargers.

short_comment: Jones (cramps) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
long_comment: Jones left the game during the fourth quarter, and given the score of the contest, the veteran linebacker is unlikely to return to Sunday's game. If that's the case, then Jones will finish with two tackles (one solo) and one QB hit.

short_comment: Spillane (illness) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
long_comment: Spillane went to the locker room in the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's international game. Darius Muasau has taken over for Spillane at inside linebacker.

short_comment: Moses (knee) has returned to Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Moses went to the locker room in the first quarter to have his knee injury evaluated. He's been cleared by medical staff to return and is back in at right tackle, with backup Caleb Lomu now on the sidelines.

short_comment: Van Roten (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
long_comment: Van Roten will be available to make his season debut after spending the first nine weeks of the campaign on injured reserve due to the hamstring issue. He was able to practice throughout Week 10 prep, turning in a pair of a limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full activity Friday, and the Patriots activated him Saturday. With Ben Brown (knee) and Walter Rouse (concussion) inactive for the Germany game, Van Roten will likely draw the start at left guard.

short_comment: Tyson caught one of two targets for six yards and added four rushing yards on his only carry in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
long_comment: One week after seeing 13 targets as Tyler Shough's top downfield option, Tyson all but disappeared as Chris Olave instead saw WR1-worthy volume. The Saints' aerial attack simply may not be able to support both wideouts in the same game, which would mark Tyson as a volatile, but high-ceiling, fantasy asset for the rest of the season. The rookie will try to bounce back in Week 12 against the Bengals.

short_comment: Etienne carried the ball 14 times for 76 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 21-13 loss to Chicago.
long_comment: The former Jaguar was the clear No. 1 option in the backfield for the Saints, Alvin Kamara saw just two touches and CJ Donaldson handled five, although Kamara did vulture another red-zone TD on a one-yard reception in the second quarter, Most of Etienne's production came on a 46-yard scamper that saw him tackled just short of the goal line, setting up Kamara's score, but the fact that he was able to produce his first big play as a Saint was still encouraging. Etienne will attempt to build on this performance in Week 12 against the Bengals.

short_comment: Shough completed 25 of 42 passes for 222 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears. He added 34 rushing yards on three carries.
long_comment: Despite the high volume of attempts, Shough couldn't get much going through the air while dealing with a ferocious Chicago pass rush that sacked him six times, including one for a fourth-quarter safety by Montez Sweat. Shough has gone four straight games without producing multiple TDs, posting a 4:3 TD:INT over that stretch while completing 67.3 percent of his passes with a weak 6.3 YPA. The second-year QB will likely need to be a lot more productive in Week 12 if the Saints are going to keep up with Joe Burrow and the Bengals.

short_comment: Olave caught nine of 15 targets for 102 yards in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
long_comment: One week after taking a back seat to rookie Jordyn Tyson, Olave re-emerged as Tyler Shough's favorite downfield option, as he set a new season high in targets and topped 100 receiving yards for the fourth time in 2026. Tyson, meanwhile, caught only one pass on two targets, suggesting the Saints' aerial attack may not be able to support both wideouts in the same game. Olave will look to make an impact again in Week 12 against the Bengals.

short_comment: Johnson injured his hamstring during Sunday's game in Chicago, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports.
long_comment: Johnson visited the sideline tent in the third quarter before the Saints deemed him questionable to return. He didn't catch his only target before his departure.

short_comment: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback against the Bears on Sunday.
long_comment: As the emergency QB3, Wilson is not allowed to play Sunday unless starter Tyler Shough and backup Spencer Rattler both leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection. Wilson has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026.

short_comment: Werner (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game against Chicago.
long_comment: Werner injured his hamstring against the Panthers in Week 10, and the injury prevented the sixth-year linebacker from practicing in any capacity during Week 11 prep. He was initially tagged as questionable, but he will observe Sunday's game from the sidelines, and his next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29. Danny Stutsman figures to start alongside Kaden Elliss at inside linebacker in Werner's absence.

short_comment: Estime (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bears.
long_comment: Estime's role in the offense was reduced in Week 10 against the Panthers, which marked Travis Etienne's return from a five-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Estime is a healthy scratch for Sunday's game, which means Alvin Kamara and CJ Donaldson will operate as the rotational options out of the backfield behind Etienne. Estime's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.

short_comment: The Saints signed Smyth to a two-year contract Saturday, Michael McQuaid of NFL Ireland reports.
long_comment: Smyth has been elevated from the Saints' practice squad for each of the team's last two games following the release of Daniel Carlson on Nov. 3. Smyth has gone 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts and 4-for-4 on extra-point tries in his two appearances, and his new deal means he'll be the Saints' kicker through the 2027 season.

short_comment: Donaldson (shoulder) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
long_comment: Donaldson missed the Saints' last three games due to a shoulder injury, but his full practice Wednesday indicates that he'll be available for Sunday's road game against the Bears. Even if Donaldson does suit up, his role in the backfield figures to be minimal, seeing as Travis Etienne is off injured reserve and Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime are also available for the Saints.

short_comment: Elliss recorded 15 tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
long_comment: Elliss was all over the field Sunday with a career-high 15 tackles (11 in the first half), which included an eight-yard sack on Bryce Young on the final play of the third quarter. Elliss has logged 10-plus tackles and a sack in back-to-back games, and the veteran linebacker is up to 56 stops (29 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass defenses across six regular-season games.

short_comment: Lance returned three kickoffs for 55 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
long_comment: The rookie fourth-rounder didn't see a target from Tyler Shough during Sunday's loss, and Lance has not recorded a catch in each of his last two outings, coinciding with the return of 2026 first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson. Lance's nine offensive snaps were a season low, and he figures to be limited to return duties now that Tyson is back in the fold. The Saints will hit the road for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

short_comment: Fant failed to haul in his lone target during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
long_comment: Fant didn't connect with Tyler Shough on a short pass late in the first quarter, and that ended up being the only target for the veteran tight end. Fant has a 12-96-3 line on 19 targets through eight regular-season games, although he's logged one reception or zero in four of his last five outings. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal as the Saints' TE2 behind Juwan Johnson heading into Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

short_comment: Vele caught both of his targets for 14 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
long_comment: Vele was on the field for 55 of the Saints' 63 offensive snaps, which was second most among wide receivers behind Chris Olave (56). Despite that playing time, Vele saw only two targets Sunday, although no other Saints pass catcher logged more than three receptions other than rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson, who finished with 11 catches on 13 targets for 80 yards. Vele has two receptions in each of his last two outings, and it appears his role in the Saints' passing offense has shrunk due to the return of Tyson. Vele will look to bounce back for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22, and Chicago's defense ranks 15th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed to receivers per game.

short_comment: Kamra rushed two times for four yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added three catches for 10 yards and an additional touchdown on four targets.
long_comment: With Travis Etienne back from his weeks-long hamstring injury that saw him miss five games while on injured reserve, the Saints deployed a three-man backfield committee against Carolina. Kamara scored a couple touchdowns, but it was a fluky performance on just five touches and 16 offensive snaps. Audric Estime logged 27 snaps and handled eight touches, while Etienne played 21 snaps and touched the ball 11 times. This is a backfield to avoid in fantasy while it the trio cancels each other out and caps each others' upside.

short_comment: The Saints placed Miller (knee) on injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Miller is dealing with a knee injury and is now required to miss at least four games. The rookie nose tackle has played in four games this season, logging five tackles (two solo) over 93 snaps on defense and four snaps on special teams. Nathan Shepherd and Khristian Boyd could both get more defensive snaps during Miller's absence.

short_comment: Edwards (knee) does not have an injury designation against the Panthers on Sunday, Ross Jackson of WWL-TV reports.
long_comment: Edwards' practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday due to a knee injury, but he avoided an injury tag for Week 10 after logging a full session Friday. He has started in each of the Saints' first eight games of the regular season.

short_comment: Banks (ankle) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Ross Jackson of WWL-TV reports.
long_comment: Banks was able to avoid an injury tag after logging a full practice Friday. Sunday's game will be his second since being activated from injured reserve Nov. 7 due to a high-ankle sprain that he suffered in Week 2 against the Ravens.

short_comment: Newsome (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday evening's matchup with the Jaguars, Patricia Traina of SI.com reports.
long_comment: Newsome suffered an ankle injury in the first quarter, and he will now officially remain sidelined for the rest of Week 11. In his absence, Paulson Adebo will continue to operate in an elevated role in New York's secondary.

short_comment: The Giants elevated Mafah from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: It's the second time this season that Mafah has been promoted to the 53-man roster, with the first instance being Week 10 against the Eagles. His elevation gives the Giants another contributor on special teams and extra depth in the backfield behind Cam Skattebo, Devin Singletary and Greg Desrosiers.

short_comment: Likely (undisclosed) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: That said, Duggan noted that he did see Likely, who hasn't been on the Giants' Week 11 injury report so far, walking into the building after the team's Friday morning walkthrough. In any case, New York's upcoming practice report will provide context regarding Likely's apparent absence, as well as his official status for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.

short_comment: Harrison (groin) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
long_comment: Harrison missed the Giants' contest versus the Commanders in Week 10 because of a groin injury, but it appears he'll be able to return to game action in Week 11. Of his 141 total snaps so far in 2026, 136 have come on special teams.

short_comment: Tracy (hamstring) could be reinstated from injured reserve when first eligible ahead of the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: The Giants haven't provided any updates on Tracy since he landed on IR on Oct. 27 after sustaining a hamstring strain in a Week 7 win over the Texans, but the running back is seemingly progressing well and could be ready to play once he sits out the required four games. Once he's reinstated, Tracy could operate as a change-of-pace option behind Cam Skattebo, who appears to have reclaimed the lead role out of the New York backfield after a one-game benching in Week 6.

short_comment: Winston carried twice for one yard in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.
long_comment: J.J. McCarthy made his third consecutive start for the Giants, but Winston continued to get sprinkled into the game plan during short-yardage situations. He extended a second-quarter drive that culminated in a Cam Skattebo touchdown by gaining a yard on a fourth-and-one play, but Winston was dropped for no gain on a third-and-one run in the fourth quarter that resulted in a Giants punt. The Giants may continue to turn to Winston for quarterback sneaks in future weeks in an effort to limit the wear and tear on McCarthy.

short_comment: Gipson was signed by the Giants off of Philadelphia's practice squad Monday, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
long_comment: Gipson will head to New York after spending the entirety of the 2026 campaign to this point on the Eagles' practice squad. The Giants waived primary kick and punt returner Charlie Jones on Monday, and Gipson will likely take over that role beginning in Week 11 against the Jaguars.

short_comment: McFadden made 10 tackles (five solo) in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
long_comment: McFadden logged one tackle for loss in the contest. The starting inside linebacker assisted the Giants in holding the Commanders to 3.2 yards per carry and no rushing touchdowns in the game.

short_comment: Holland logged three tackles (one solo) and one pass defensed for an interception in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
long_comment: Holland picked off Jayden Daniels with 2:19 left in the fourth quarter, just one Commanders drive after Ar'Darius Washington picked the quarterback off. Despite back-to-back turnovers, the Giants' offense logged back-to-back three-and-outs to put the Commanders' offense in position to win the game.

short_comment: Washington accumulated seven tackles (five solo) and two passes defensed, including one interception, in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
long_comment: Washington broke up two passes in the contest, picking off Jayden Daniels with 5:31 left in the fourth quarter of Thursday's game. Despite making a crucial play with the Giants up four points, the offense could not put more points on the board to cement a primetime win.

short_comment: Reese logged 13 tackles (four solo) in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
long_comment: Reese led the Giants in tackles as a consistent force against the Commanders' run game in the NFC East showdown. Despite the rookie first-rounder's best efforts, the Giants allowed 24 points en route to a meaningful divisional loss.

short_comment: Zvada missed his only field-goal try and made all three of his PATs on Thursday in a loss to Washington.
long_comment: Zvada's miss was a chip-shot 33-yarder in the first quarter that sailed wide left. That proved to be a critical mistake, as the Commanders won by just three points. Zvada appeared to shore up his job security a bit by going 4-for-4 on FG tries in Week 9 against Philadelphia, but it's hard to ignore the fact that he's gone just 17-for-23 on field-goal attempts overall and has missed three kicks from under 50 yards. The rookie does have a perfect 16-for-16 mark on extra-point attempts, and head coach John Harbaugh expressed support for the inconsistent kicker Friday, saying of Zvada, "I'm confident that he's going to become a good kicker. If at some point and time it doesn't happen, it doesn't happen. But I'm not going to panic halfway through the season with a guy who has made a bunch of kicks," Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.

short_comment: Johnson logged one catch (on three targets) for eight yards Thursday in a loss to the Commanders.
long_comment: Johnson hasn't been able to get going in 2026, as he's finished with one or zero catches in six of his seven games so far. After working as New York's top tight end last season, he's been mostly an afterthought in the current campaign due to the arrival of Isaiah Likely, who went off for a 9-127-1 line on a team-leading 11 targets Thursday. As long as Likely is healthy, Johnson won't have much appeal in most fantasy formats.

short_comment: Mooney caught two of five targets for eight yards Thursday in a loss to Washington.
long_comment: Mooney logged the third-most targets of any New York pass catcher, but he managed just two short receptions. Efficiency has been an issue for the veteran wideout throughout the campaign, as he's hauled in only 14 of 30 targets through nine contests. Mooney has finished with fewer than 10 yards in four of his past six appearances, so he's not a viable fantasy play at the moment.

short_comment: Singletary played just five snaps on offense and took one carry for three yards in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.
long_comment: Cam Skattebo came back from a hamstring injury and dominated backfield work, taking 21 touches for 122 yards and two touchdowns on an 88 percent snap share. Singletary played 92 percent of snaps the week before in a win at Philadelphia, but his 23 touches went for just 39 total yards and no TDs. It'll likely be another large workload for Skattebo when the Giants host the Jaguars in Week 11.

short_comment: Parham (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Amanda Vogt of the Jets' official site reports.
long_comment: Parham, who is working through a knee issue, has been given the green light to play Sunday after going through pregame warmups. He'll start at left guard while Jordan Meredith provides depth at the position.

short_comment: Wallace (groin) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Amanda Vogt of the Jets' official site reports.
long_comment: Wallace will end up missing a third consecutive game due to a groin injury, and his next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Dolphins on Nov. 29. He's mostly operated on special teams this season, but his absence means the Jets will have less depth at the edge rusher position for Sunday's contest.

short_comment: Phillips (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Amanda Vogt of the Jets' official site reports.
long_comment: Phillips played through an ankle issue against the Bills in Week 10, and the veteran defensive tackle has been cleared to suit up for Sunday's contest. He has accumulated 36 tackles (11 solo) and one fumble recovery through 10 regular-season games.

short_comment: The Jets elevated Shepard from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: The move gives the Jets much-needed depth at wide receiver given the absences of both Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) for Sunday's game against the Chargers. It will be the third elevation of the season for Shepard and first since Week 4 against the Bears, so he would need to be signed to the 53-man roster in order to suit up for the Jets beyond Week 11.

short_comment: Head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters Friday that Hall could see a bump in touches for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Howie Kussoy of the New York Post reports.
long_comment: "Obviously, [Hall] and Garrett Wilson are guys that we really try to target for the most part...Hall will end up getting a tick more [touches] because, again, he's our starting running back," Glenn said Friday. In his two outings since returning from a five-game absence due to a quad injury, Hall has turned 26 carries into 102 yards (3.9 YPC) while catching seven of eight passes for 93 yards, and he topped 100 scrimmage yards against the Bills in Week 10. Braelon Allen has reverted to RB2 duties in Hall's return, but the former has still been efficient with his touches and is still firmly in the mix for touches despite the return of Hall. The duo will face a Chargers defense Sunday that ranks 15th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (110.2) and limited Derrick Henry to 10 yards on 10 carries (albeit with two touchdowns) in a 23-20 win over the Ravens in Week 10.

short_comment: Onyemata (abdomen) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
long_comment: Onyemata was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday and strung together three consecutive limited practice sessions. However, the veteran defensive tackle is not quite ready to come off IR, so his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 29. Onyemata has not played since Week 2 against the Packers due to an abdominal injury.

short_comment: Smith (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
long_comment: Smith dealt with an ankle injury during the week after he was forced from last Sunday's loss against the Bills, but all scans came back clean, and the veteran quarterback is good to go for a road date in Los Angeles. Smith has been able to get the ball to his playmakers this season, but he doesn't have any fantasy upside as a statuesque pocket passer in an offense that likes to run the ball.

short_comment: With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Taylor could see more pass-catching opportunities Sunday against the Chargers.
long_comment: Isaiah Williams (ribs) also has been ruled out for the Jets, so they'll be down their Nos. 3 and 4 receivers, which could lead to more multiple-tight end sets for New York. Taylor is averaging 2.8 catches for 20.9 yards per game this season. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.

short_comment: With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Sadiq could see more pass-catching opportunities Sunday against the Chargers.
long_comment: In addition to Cooper, Isaiah Williams (ribs) also will be sidelined against Los Angeles. Sadiq could essentially handle WR3 duties behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, though it's not the easiest matchup against the Los Angeles defense. Sadiq has a chance to see elevated snaps, which could translate to more targets in the passing game, but he's still difficult to get behind as a fantasy starter.

short_comment: With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, Mitchell is expected to play an elevated role on offense Sunday against the Chargers.
long_comment: Cooper was injured early in last Sunday's loss to the Bills, and Mitchell went on to see eight targets, as the Jets were playing catch-up most of the afternoon. They might be able to keep things closer against the 1-8 Chargers, though Los Angeles is still favored in the contest. Mitchell is a big-play threat as a WR4 for fantasy purposes.

short_comment: Belton finished Sunday's loss to the Bills with six tackles (one solo) and one defensed pass.
long_comment: Belton tied for third on the Jets with six stops. That's a total he's now reached in every game this season except Week 1. Belton ranks second among NFL safeties with 82 tackles on the campaign.

short_comment: Davis posted six tackles (three solo) Sunday in a loss to Buffalo.
long_comment: Davis' six tackles tied for third-most on the Jets. The veteran linebacker has been relatively consistent this season with between six and 10 stops in seven of his 10 games so far. Davis has 68 total tackles (including 2.0 sacks) through 10 games, putting him on pace for a 10th consecutive triple-digit tackle campaign.

short_comment: Sherwood secured nine tackles (four solo) in Sunday's Week 10 loss to the Bills.
long_comment: Sherwood finished second on the Jets in stops Sunday, behind Harrison Phillips (10). Sherwood has notched at least eight tackles in five straight games, and he's hit the double-digit mark three times this season. The veteran linebacker ranks eighth in the NFL with 86 tackles through 10 games.

short_comment: Sanders made all four of his field-goal attempts in the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
long_comment: Sanders knocked in field goals from 41, 27, 22 and 48 yards out in Sunday's contest. The kicker accounted for all 12 of the Jets' points for a second straight week, performing the same feat in the team's Week 9 loss to the Chiefs. Sanders moves to 25-for-28 on field-goal attempts over nine contests so far during the 2026 season.

short_comment: Davis didn't touch the ball on offense in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
long_comment: With Breece Hall and Braelon Allen both healthy, Davis has minimal fantasy value, except for leagues that count return yardage. He's played zero offensive snaps over the last two contests, but Davis did return three kickoffs for 74 yards against Buffalo.

short_comment: Allen rushed eight times for 40 yards and caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
long_comment: For a second consecutive game, Allen was outplayed by Breece Hall, who produced 108 scrimmage yards on 15 touches. Allen remains the more efficient runner, averaging 5.0 yards per carry to Hall's 3.4 this season, but Hall is the team's preferred option in passing situations, which have been plentiful with the 2-8 Jets frequently in catch-up mode. Perhaps a Week 11 matchup with a Chargers team that's still searching for its first win through Sunday of Week 10 will offer an opportunity to stick with the run and play to Allen's strengths.

short_comment: Klubnik completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. He added three rushing attempts for 26 yards.
long_comment: Klubnik saw the first regular-season action of his NFL career in the second half of Sunday's loss, as Geno Smith (ankle) exited the game. The rookie fourth-round pick led the offense down to Buffalo's four-yard line on his first possession in the third quarter, but the Jets settled for a field goal on that possession, and Klubnik was picked off on his next drive. If Smith isn't ready to return in Week 11, Klubnik would be in line to make his first regular-season start on the road against the Chargers.

short_comment: Wilson (concussion) caught seven of 14 targets for 106 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
long_comment: Wilson set a new season high in targets and came one yard short of his Week 3 season high Sunday in his return from a one-game absence due to a concussion. His production came on a mix of passes from Geno Smith (ankle) and rookie Cade Klubnik, the latter of whom saw his first NFL action after Smith exited in the second half. Wilson figures to work as the top target for whomever starts under center in a Week 11 road game against the Chargers.

short_comment: Barkley (left arm) said after Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers that he believes he'll play in Thursday's game at Dallas, Johnny McGonigal of PennLive.com reports.
long_comment: Barkley didn't log a touch after the 8:02 mark of the fourth quarter after he had an apparent left arm injury examined by team trainers, according to Olivia Reiner of The Philadelphia Inquirer. While Barkley wouldn't elaborate on the issue to McGonigal, the running back seemed optimistic about his chances to suit up in Week 12. Barkley finished Sunday's matchup with 17 carries for 75 yards and one touchdown and wasn't targeted by QB Joe Milton. Monday's injury report may provide further clarity on Barkley's situation.

short_comment: Smith (hamstring) caught five of 12 targets for 41 yards in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.
long_comment: Smith was targeted on 12 of Joe Milton's 21 passes in the wide receiver's first game since Week 6. Milton has thrown for just 310 yards without a touchdown pass through two starts for the Eagles, so expectations should be tempered for the team's entire passing game, but Smith has reclaimed his role as the team's top pass catcher. Smith could make the most of his hefty target share Thursday against the generous Dallas secondary.

short_comment: Jones (foot) was spotted in a walking boot following Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
long_comment: Jones is dealing with an apparent right foot injury after recording five total tackles (two solo) and three passes defensed during the team's Week 11 victory. More information on his status will likely come when the Eagles return to practice Wednesday.

short_comment: Mitchell (hamstring) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Steelers.
long_comment: Mitchell injured his left hamstring in the second half, and medical staff have determined that the injury is severe enough for the third-year defensive back to be sidelined for the remainder of Sunday's contest. Riq Woolen will take over at cornerback the rest of the way.

short_comment: Shipley (foot) is active for Sunday's game against Pittsburgh.
long_comment: Shipley was activated from injured reserve Saturday, and the third-year running back has been officially cleared to return from a four-game absence due to a partial plantar fascia tear that he sustained in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Shipley and Jaydon Blue will operate as the Eagles' rotational running backs behind Saquon Barkley for Sunday's game against a Steelers defense that ranks third in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (83.2).

short_comment: Mondon (ankle) is inactive for Sunday's matchup against Pittsburgh.
long_comment: Mondon was deemed doubtful entering the weekend after not practicing Thursday or Friday following Philadelphia's Week 10 bye. He could have seen more action on defense after Zack Baun (back) landed on IR on Saturday, but Mondon will instead miss his first game of the campaign. Jeremiah Trotter and Jihaad Campbell figure to be the Eagles' starting inside linebackers Sunday.

short_comment: Payton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Eagles' emergency third quarterback against the Steelers on Sunday.
long_comment: As the emergency third quarterback, Payton is not allowed to play Sunday unless both starter Joe Milton and backup Tanner McKee are taken out of the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

short_comment: Carter (quadriceps) is active for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
long_comment: Carter informed the Eagles' medical staff while he was traveling to the stadium Sunday that his quadriceps was bothering him. The fifth-year defensive tackle has been cleared to suit up, but if he plays under a snap count or is available only as an emergency option, then Ty Robinson and Gabe Hall would be poised to take on larger roles on defense.

short_comment: Baun (back) was placed on the Eagles' injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Baun was held out of practice all week due to a back injury that he sustained against the Giants in Week 9. The injury is severe enough for him to require a stint on IR, which means he'll miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against the Seahawks. Jeremiah Trotter figures to start alongside Jihaad Campbell at inside linebacker moving forward, beginning with Sunday's home tilt against the Steelers.

short_comment: The Eagles placed Wicks (ankle/foot) on injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Wicks missed the three games before the Eagles' Week 10 bye due to an ankle injury, and he was limited during Week 11 prep before the team tacked on a foot issue on Friday's practice report, after which he was ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Steelers. Per Tim McManus of ESPN.com, Wicks sustained the foot injury Friday, and it presumably led to his placement on IR. Wicks will be sidelined until at least Philadelphia's Week 15 matchup with Seattle on Saturday, Dec. 19.

short_comment: Carter (abdomen) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Steelers.
long_comment: An abdominal injury prevented Carter from playing in Week 9 against the Giants. He had extra rest thanks to the Week 10 bye, and his full practice Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. Carter's return gives the Eagles a boost in the secondary and another contributor on special teams.

short_comment: Smith (illness) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against Pittsburgh.
long_comment: An illness limited Smith's practice reps both Wednesday and Thursday, but he was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. The fourth-year edge rusher has 17 tackles (nine solo), including 5.0 sacks, and one pass defense across eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Covey (knee) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
long_comment: Covey was a limited participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep, but the veteran wide receiver has done enough to be cleared to return from a two-game absence due to a knee injury. He'll likely operate as the Eagles' top return option on kickoffs and punts while providing depth at wide receiver.

short_comment: Lemon will operate as the Eagles' WR2 against the Steelers on Sunday due to the return of DeVonta Smith (hamstring).
long_comment: Smith has missed five of the Eagles' last six games (and each of the last three contests) due to a hamstring injury, but the veteran wide receiver does not carry an injury designation heading into the weekend. Lemon has been the team's WR1 in Smith's absence, but the former still will be heavily involved in the offensive game plan given that Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) has been ruled out for a fourth consecutive game. Joe Milton is getting the start at quarterback for a second straight contest, and the Eagles are facing a Steelers defense that ranks 30th in the NFL in receiving yards allowed per game (260.6). Over his last five outings, Lemon has put together a 27-247-1 line on 39 targets.

short_comment: Campbell (hamstring/quadriceps) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
long_comment: Campbell was sidelined for each of the Eagles' two contests prior to the Week 10 bye due to hamstring and quadriceps injuries. The second-year linebacker made the most of the extra rest courtesy of the bye, and he is on track to return against the Steelers on Sunday.

short_comment: McKee will remain in a backup role for Sunday's game against the Steelers after head coach Nick Sirianni announced Wednesday that Joe Milton will serve as the Eagles' starting quarterback for a second straight game, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
long_comment: Though the Eagles dropped a seventh straight game while Milton turned the ball over once and took seven sacks in a Week 9 loss to the Giants, Sirianni saw enough from the third-year signal-caller to hand him at least one more start. While it's conceivable that the Eagles could go back to McKee -- who started Weeks 6 through 8 -- at some point if Milton's performance isn't up to par, rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton is also on the roster and may get a look before the season winds down.

short_comment: Head coach Nick Sirianni confirmed that Milton will remain the Eagles' starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Steelers, according to NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano.
long_comment: While starting in his team debut Week 9 against the Giants, Milton was unable to bring an end to the Eagles' lengthy losing streak, but the third-year quarterback showed enough positives to retain the starting gig coming out of a Week 10 bye. Milton put an intriguing dual-threat skill set on display with 64 yards on nine carries to go with 169 passing yards on 34 attempts in the 19-11 loss to New York, with the rushing output in particular perhaps making him worth a look in superflex leagues or leagues that start two quarterbacks. He lost a fumble and took seven sacks in the loss to the Giants, so Milton may need to show that he can avoid negative plays in Week 11 in order to guarantee himself additional starts.

short_comment: The Eagles signed Blue from their practice squad to their active roster Tuesday.
long_comment: It's already the third time this season Blue has been signed by Philadelphia from the practice squad to the active roster. The second-year pro has seen action in two games with the club, recording a nine-yard catch on his only touch while racking up 268 yards on 12 kickoff returns. Blue is currently the only healthy running back on the Eagles' active roster aside from starter Saquon Barkley, but that may change soon, as Will Shipley (foot - IR) had his practice window opened Monday. Elijah Mitchell has been promoted from the practice squad to help in the backfield each of the past three weeks, so he'd need to be signed to the active roster as well in order to suit up against Pittsburgh this Sunday.

short_comment: The Eagles signed Ertz from the practice squad to the active roster Monday.
long_comment: Philadelphia is coming off a Week 10 bye, but prior to the midseason respite, there were no reported injuries in the TE group on the active roster. When the position group was depleted earlier this season, the team used elevations on Ertz from Weeks 3-5, but his snap share decreased game by game (38, 21 and 11 percent), while he hauled in three of eight targets for 22 yards in that span. Wednesday's practice report will reveal if any of Dallas Goedert, Eli Stowers, Johnny Mundt or Grant Calcaterra are banged up at the moment.

short_comment: Trotter recorded 11 tackles (five solo) and one forced fumble during the Eagles' 19-11 loss to the Giants in Week 9.
long_comment: Trotter was on the field for 64 of the Eagles' 67 defensive snaps (95.5 percent), and he was the only Philadelphia defender to reach double-digit stops. He's tallied at least 10 tackles three times in 2026, and the third-year pro is up to 51 tackles (32 solo), including 0.5 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Moore caught one of two targets for minus-3 yards during the Eagles' 19-11 loss to the Giants on Sunday.
long_comment: Week 9 was the Eagles' first game with Joe Milton as the starter, with Tanner McKee relegated to backup duties. Milton completed 18 of his 34 passes, and his lone connection with Moore resulted in a three-yard loss. The Eagles are on a bye for Week 10, and Moore's role on the offense would evaporate if one or both of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) or Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was cleared to play in Week 11 against the Steelers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

short_comment: Cooper caught just two of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
long_comment: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) still out, Cooper played more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps for the third straight game. He's done very little with that playing time, producing five catches for 61 yards during that span. Cooper is well off the fantasy radar until he shows something in the box score, and that's if Smith and Wicks remain sidelined.

short_comment: Rodgers completed 30 of 44 passes for 227 yards and one touchdown while rushing five times for 29 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
long_comment: Rodgers threw a 20-yard touchdown pass to Max Hurleman on Pittsburgh's final offensive play with 1:21 remaining in the fourth quarter, but that was too little too late, as the Eagles proceeded to run out the clock to drop the Steelers to 6-4. Hurleman stepped up down the stretch in his first NFL game after starting wide receiver DK Metcalf was disqualified. Rodgers had a four-game stretch in which he threw 11 touchdown passes while posting at least 235 passing yards in each outing, but he has failed to reach that yardage total in any of his last four starts while recording only four TDs during the latter stretch. Snapping out of this recent funk won't be easy for Rodgers against the stout Broncos defense Friday.

short_comment: Dowdle rushed five times for 15 yards and caught four of five targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
long_comment: Dowdle finished with 34 scrimmage yards for a second consecutive game after racking up 235 scrimmage yards over his preceding four appearances. He had five more yards than Jaylen Warren on two fewer touches in Sunday's loss. Dowdle is poised to retain his spot as the 1B option alongside Warren in Friday's Week 12 home game against the Broncos.

short_comment: Warren rushed nine times for 28 yards and caught two of three targets for one yard in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
long_comment: Warren finished with 29 yards on 11 touches compared to 34 yards on nine touches for Rico Dowdle, as Pittsburgh's backfield duo was held quiet for a second consecutive game. After recording at least 73 scrimmage yards in eight consecutive games to start the season, Warren has produced just 75 yards without a touchdown over the past two games. Warren and Dowdle should continue to split backfield touches Friday against the Broncos.

short_comment: Metcalf was ejected in the third quarter of Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: After accruing his second unsportsmanlike penalty of the contest, Metcalf was tossed from this Week 11 matchup. Prior to his exit with 4:58 remaining in the third quarter, he was having his least productive performance of the season (1-2-0 receiving line on four targets). The Steelers will roll with Germie Bernard, Roman Wilson, Ben Skowronek and Max Hurleman at wide receiver with Metcalf unavailable for the rest of the game.

short_comment: Highsmith (ankle) has been ruled out from returning to Sunday's matchup against Philadelphia, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Highsmith began the game with a flourish, recording 2.0 sacks in the first quarter. However, he injured his ankle during that opening period and isn't going to be able to re-enter the contest. Jack Sawyer will likely log more defensive snaps with Highsmith sidelined.

short_comment: Wetjen (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
long_comment: Wetjen has operated as the Steelers' top returner on both kickoffs and punts this season. However, with Roman Wilson back from injured reserve and Max Hurleman elevated from the practice squad to the active roster, Wetjen will be a healthy scratch Sunday for the first time this season. Wetjen's next opportunity to play is Friday against the Broncos, although the rookie fourth-rounder's chances of suiting up for that contest would be further diminished if Michael Pittman (foot) is activated from IR before that game.

short_comment: Queen (hand) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
long_comment: Queen was working through a hand injury during Week 11 prep, but the veteran linebacker has been given the green light by medical staff to play Sunday. He has logged double-digit tackles in each of his last three outings and is up to 74 tackles (25 solo), including 3.5 sacks, four pass defenses (including an interception) and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Elliott (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
long_comment: Elliott did not play in Week 10 against the Bengals due to a knee injury he sustained during pregame warmups. He drew the questionable tag for Week 11 after logging full practices Thursday and Friday, and he's been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday. Elliott's return means Robert Spears-Jennings will revert to a rotational role in the secondary.

short_comment: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Steelers' emergency quarterback against the Eagles on Sunday.
long_comment: As has been the case all year, Howard will be the emergency QB3 behind starter Aaron Rodgers and backup Mason Rudolph. As such, Howard is not allowed to see the field Sunday unless both Rodgers and Rudolph leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

short_comment: Wilson (hand/finger) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
long_comment: The third-year wideout was activated from injured reserve Saturday, foreshadowing his availability for Sunday's contest following a four-game absence. Wilson recorded at least three receptions in his first four games of the season on his way to a 14-188-2 line on 25 targets, and he then failed to reel in the only pass thrown his way in Week 5 against the Colts before exiting that game at halftime with his injury. In his return Sunday against Philadelphia, Wilson should slot into the No. 3 receiver role behind DK Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard, the latter who leapfrogged Wilson on the depth chart over the last several games while filling in for both him and Michael Pittman (IR, foot).

short_comment: The Steelers elevated Hurleman from the practice squad Saturday.
long_comment: With Michael Pittman (foot) remaining on injured reserve and Roman Wilson (finger) officially listed as questionable, Hurleman is up as the Steelers' sixth receiver. He's never appeared in a regular-season NFL game.

short_comment: Pittman (foot) is not expected to be activated from injured reserve for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Brooke Pryor of ESPN reports.
long_comment: Pittman was able to practice fully both Thursday and Friday, but he is not ready to rejoin the mix just yet -- which Pittsburgh confirmed by omitting Pittman from the list of roster moves it made Saturday. Barring an unannounced setback, Pittman figures to continue practicing, and his next chance to take the field will arrive Black Friday, when the Steelers square off against the Broncos.

short_comment: Herbig (hip) has been downgraded from questionable to out for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Burt Lauten of the Steelers' official site reports.
long_comment: A hip injury prevented Herbig from participating in any of the Steelers' three practice sessions during Week 11 prep. The door was left ajar for him to play Sunday, but he'll observe the game from the sidelines, and his absence means Jack Sawyer will operate in an elevated role at edge rusher behind starters Alex Highsmith and T.J. Watt. Herbig's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Broncos on Friday.

short_comment: The Steelers designated Dunker (knee) for return to practice from injured reserve Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Dunker went to IR with a sprained MCL back in late September, but it now looks like he's close to being available again. The move opens a 21-day window during which Pittsburgh can officially activate him before he'd have to go back on the shelf for the remainder of the campaign.

short_comment: The Steelers placed McCormick (ankle) on injured reserve Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: McCormick dislocated his ankle during the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday. The good news for the third-year pro is that he avoided a fracture and does not require surgery, so there's a chance he could return for the Steelers should the team qualify for the playoffs, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Brock Hoffman figures to start at left guard in McCormick's stead.

short_comment: Brisker notched 10 tackles (two solo) Sunday in a Week 10 loss to the Bengals.
long_comment: Pittsburgh gave up 38 points, so it wasn't exactly a stellar performance by the team's defense. However, three different Steelers players logged double-digit tackles -- including Brisker, who finished with 10. That's a season-high mark for the veteran safety, who has finished with at least six stops in all but one of his nine games so far this season.

short_comment: Wilson recorded 19 tackles (nine solo) in Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
long_comment: Wilson not only set a career high with his 19 stops, he also tied the NFL high mark by any player so far this season. The third-year linebacker has jumped up a notch as an IDP asset in 2026, as he's tied for sixth in the league with 88 stops through nine games. Wilson has also added a sack, three defensed passes (including one interception) and a fumble recovery.

short_comment: Boswell made his sole field-goal attempt and sole PAT in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
long_comment: Boswell had an uneventful night, making his 45-yard field goal in the second quarter of the contest. The kicker moves to 19-for-24 on field-goal attempts and 17-for-17 on PATs over nine regular-season games in 2026.

short_comment: Bernard failed to reel in any of his three targets while notching a 10-yard rush during Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
long_comment: Bernard went without a catch for the first time since Week 1, and his three targets were his fewest since the team's Week 4 loss to the Browns. The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track in Week 11 versus the Eagles.

short_comment: Washington caught one pass for five yards on two targets in Sunday night's loss to the Bengals.
long_comment: Aaron Rodgers threw for 143 yards in the game, and most of that came in garbage time in the second half with the score already out of hand. Washington has fewer than 30 receiving yards in seven of nine games played this season and is the epitome of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at tight end.

short_comment: Rudolph completed one of three pass attempts for two yards and rushed once for nine yards in Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
long_comment: After the Bengals had built a 20-point lead with five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, head coach Mike McCarthy opted to remove starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers from the game and turned to Rudolph to direct the offense for the Steelers' final possession. Rudolph led the Steelers on an 11-play drive that concluded in the red zone before time expired. The 31-year-old Rudolph has now made four relief appearances behind Rodgers on the season, playing limited snaps in each of those contests.
